The direct route sent the dialog's standard quality (10) and the tab had no Canon quality row, so a chart could not be printed in the state his photos get. The row now lists the qualities the driver's own dialog allows for the chosen paper (Canon: the model's media database, XML or binary; Epson: the `Resolution` table of PDEData.dat), and preselects the quality of his last print on that paper through the macOS dialog (the learning store, `workflow/printer_memory.py`), otherwise the dialog's standard. Under the row: the headline in bold, then line 1 on the next line; line 2 is added when the preselected quality came from that last dialog print. Lines 3 and 4 mark two entries of the list; {quality} is the driver's own name for the quality (“Fine”, “Normal(Fine)”, “High Quality”). A printer whose driver ChromIQ cannot read keeps its generic row, without these lines. The behaviour is Basti's; the words are ours.*

> **Print your photos at this quality too**
>
> The profile fits only prints made at the quality its chart was printed with.
> Chosen as in your last print on this paper through the macOS print dialog.
> {quality} (highest)
> {quality} (standard)

### M-SPOT-CR30-GONE · APPROVED · the CR30 stopped answering during a spot session — Tools ▸ Read single patches

**Approved by:** Basti, 2026-10-10, in the session after the review of beta 17: the wording as it stands, and his confirmation that one short press of the button switches a CR30 on, which line 3 tells the user to do.

*New message (beta 17, 2026-10-09). Basti, on beta 16: the CR30 switched itself off during a session, Stop did nothing, and once it was switched on again nothing happened until the window was closed. Nothing in the session watched the Bluetooth link, so a gone instrument looked exactly like one nobody had pressed yet. The link is now watched, Stop ends the session at once, and when the instrument goes away the session pauses and asks.*

*Every reading already in the list is kept on both answers. "Reconnect" looks for the instrument again (the remembered Bluetooth address first, then a search) and the session carries on; if it is still not there, this window comes back. The instrument's own error text goes to the window's notes and the log, not into the window.*

> **Your CR30 is not answering**
>
> ChromIQ has lost the connection to your CR30. Usually it has switched itself off to save its battery, its USB cable has come out, or it is out of Bluetooth range.
>
> Every reading in this window is kept.
>
> Switch the instrument on again (press its button once) or plug it back in, then choose “Reconnect”. ChromIQ looks for it and you carry on reading. If it is still not there, this window comes back.
>
> To finish instead, choose “Stop session”. Your readings stay in the list either way.

*Buttons: **Reconnect** (default) and **Stop session**.*

### M-SPOT-CR30-EARLY-PRESS · APPROVED · a press from before Ready was not used — Tools ▸ Read single patches, CR30

**Approved by:** Basti, 2026-10-10: both lines, the one-press and the {n}-press variant, in the English as written; the place, the window's log, unchanged.

*New 2026-10-10 (review of beta 17). The review found that a press of the CR30's button made right after the spot window said Ready was thrown away: over Bluetooth the session's read began by dropping every press the instrument had announced so far, and it began up to about a second after Ready was shown. The log said "discarded 1 reading taken before this patch was armed"; the window said nothing. Fixed: the stale presses are dropped once, BEFORE the window says Ready, and never again while the session runs, so every press made once Ready is shown is taken (over USB nothing was dropped). A press the instrument announced before Ready, typically while the calibration's last window, which itself says to press the button, was still open, is still not used, because it belongs to no reading anybody asked for; this is what the window's log then says, so nobody waits for a row that will not come. Line 1 for one press, line 2 for more. The headline names the case in the model and is not shown. It speaks through the window's log, which is visible for the whole of a CR30 session.*

> **A reading taken before Ready was not used**
>
> One reading was taken before this window was ready for it, so it was not used. Take the reading again.
> {n} readings were taken before this window was ready for them, so they were not used. Take the reading again.

### M-PROFILE-INSTALL-REPLACE · APPROVED · a profile of the same file name is already installed — every Install button

**Approved by:** Basti, 2026-10-11 (the design and these words; not asked of Knut).

*Knut, #182 [6102031563](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6102031563) answer 3, to "Installing replaces an installed profile of the same name without asking. Should ChromIQ ask first?": "Yes. Ask if user wants to replace existing or cancel to rename the profile before trying to install it again." Asked by every Install button before it writes anything (Build Profile, Apply Calibration, Check & Refine's "Install Profile As Is", the scanner window; `ui/install_profile.ask_install_path`), only when a profile of the same file name is in the profile folder. Basti's design (2026-10-11): an editable field holding the current name, the extension (.icc or .icm) beside it and kept. While the name is unchanged the button reads **Replace** and overwrites the installed profile; once it is edited the button reads **Install** and installs under the new name; if the new name is installed too, the line under the field says so and the button reads **Replace** again. **Cancel** installs nothing. Only the INSTALLED copy takes the new name; the profile in the project keeps its name (runs link to it). With "Name the installed copy after the description" ticked, the installed copy's description follows the new name too. A name may not be empty, contain / \ : * ? " < > | or a control character, begin with a dot, or be longer than 100 characters (other letters, accents and scripts are fine); the line under the field says which, and the button is off until the name is usable. Replace / Install is the default button (Return), Cancel is Escape and the close button: the person has just pressed Install and the field holds the name they keep or have typed.*

*The lines under the field: "Type a name for the installed profile.", "A name cannot contain / \ : * ? " < > | or begin with a dot.", "A name can have at most {n} characters.", "A profile named {name} is installed too. Replace overwrites it."*

*PROPOSED line, 4.3.8 beta 3 (K2), shown in the beta, wording awaiting approval: when the name is installed with the OTHER extension (X.icm installed, X.icc being installed, or the other way round; Basti, 2026-10-21: the same stem is the same name), the line under the field says which file that is, because the field shows this profile's own: "The profile installed under this name is {other}. Replace removes it and installs this profile as {name} instead, so only one profile of this name stays installed."*

> **A profile with this name is already installed**
>
> Keep the name to replace the installed profile, or give this profile another name.

### M-PRINT-VERIFY-ROUTE · APPROVED · what a verification print needs, the Print Chart tab, macOS, B3 (4.3.4 beta 1)

**Approved by:** Basti, 2026-10-10 ("text approved", the wording of review R3 below, verbatim).

*Where it is shown (B5, 2026-10-10): on the Print Chart tab, under its notice, on macOS, when the run type is Verification and a chart is loaded; on both routes, because paragraphs 1 and 3 are about which route to print by and hold whichever route is set. Paragraph 2 is about the macOS print dialog and is shown only while “Use default macOS printer dialog” is on. The headline is shown in bold above the paragraphs.*

*New 2026-10-10. Knut, #182 [6095262115](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6095262115): with Run type Verification and the macOS print dialog on, the notice on the Print Chart tab "seems to describe a profiling run, not a verification run". It is the one notice of the macOS dialog route, the same for every run type; neither §M nor `verification_printing_and_target.md` has a text for a verification print. Measured for this proposal (report folder `2026-10-10_434b1_B3`, capture queues with a generic PostScript PPD and a profile assigned in ColorSync, as on Knut's HP CLJ5550): the chart's numbers reach the printer unchanged on both routes, 1,372,807 of 1,372,807 chart pixels identical, with the dialog's Color Matching panel left alone and with another profile chosen in it, because ChromIQ gives the chart whichever profile the job prints with; but the dialog route hands a PostScript printer the chart as calibrated RGB (CIEBasedABC) and the direct route as device RGB, which a PostScript interpreter renders differently (Ghostscript: 2.3 levels mean, 26 max, on the patches). Proposed to be shown under the Print Chart tab's notice for a verification run on macOS, both routes; the second paragraph only on the dialog route. Not shown anywhere until approved.* *(Approved 2026-10-10, see above.)*

*Review R3, 2026-10-10 (report folder `2026-10-10_434b1_R3`): Sebastian approved this text on condition that every statement in it is true. Two were not. Choices made in the dialog's own Color Matching sheet (driven on screen, not injected into the settings) left the chart unchanged on a PostScript queue with a ColorSync profile, a Canon PRO-300 and an Epson ET-8550 (another profile picked; the vendor's matching chosen on the PostScript queue and the Canon), but the Epson's "EPSON colour matching" reaches the job as EPIJ_OSColMat=1, which ChromIQ neither sets back nor checks, so "Choosing another profile there does not apply it to the chart either" could not be kept as a promise about the panel. And on a generic CMYK raster queue (the CUPS sample HP DeskJet driver) with a ColorSync profile, macOS ignores the output intent and converts from the chart's tag, so the re-tag changes the raster: "If its Color Matching panel names a profile, ChromIQ gives the chart that same profile … so macOS does not change the chart's colours" is untrue there. The second paragraph now names only the printers where it was measured, and the third says what the PostScript stream carries (a CIEBasedABC colour space with sRGB's D65 white point and Rec. 709 matrix) instead of "calibrated RGB". Back to Sebastian in these words; approved by him as worded, 2026-10-10.*

> **Printing a verification chart**
>
> Print this chart on the same printer, paper, media type and quality as the profiling chart this profile was made from, and by the same route (the macOS print dialog, or straight to the printer). The profile describes the printer only in that state.
>
> Leave the colour settings in the macOS print dialog as they are, including its Color Matching panel. When macOS prints the job with a Canon or Epson paper profile, or with a profile set for a PostScript printer in ColorSync Utility, ChromIQ gives the chart that same profile after you close the dialog, so macOS does not change the chart’s colours.
>
> On a PostScript printer the two routes do not reach the printer in the same form: the dialog sends the chart’s colour values marked as sRGB, which the printer converts with its own colour rendering, and the direct route sends them as the printer’s own RGB. Print the profiling chart and its verification charts the same way.

*The wording proposed by k81, for the record:* "This sheet is printed through this run’s profile, and ChromIQ converts it through that profile itself before the dialog opens. ### M-PRINT-INKS-CONVERTED · APPROVED · the direct route, a chart that is not RGB on a queue whose driver takes RGB raster, 4.3.5 B2

**Approved by:** Basti, 2026-10-11 ("approved if every statement is true"). Checked by the combined review of 4.3.5 (report folder `2026-10-11_435_combined_review`) against the capture runs of builder round B2 (`2026-10-10_435_B2/runs/nonrgb_table.md`): every chart that is not RGB, sent by the direct route to an RGB raster queue (Gutenprint RGB), reached the printer as RGB raster with only 31 to 41 % of its patches within one level of the ink values the chart asks for, so macOS did convert it and the driver gets RGB; `ppd_color.ink_route` says "converted" only where every print-data filter takes CUPS raster in an RGB colour space. Asked and said since then (`tab_print._ask_ink_conversion`, `_report_job_ticket`).


*New 2026-10-10 (4.3.5 B2, report folder `2026-10-10_435_B2`). Basti asked to be told "when a CMYK/multi-ink chart goes to an RGB-raster queue (macOS converts it)". Asked on the direct route ("Use default macOS printer dialog" off; the dialog route refuses every chart that is not RGB) before the job is sent, with "Print Anyway" and "Cancel" (Cancel the default), when the chart is not RGB in its file and its ink list (`chart_inks`) and the queue's PPD sends every print-data filter CUPS raster in an RGB colour space for this job (`ppd_color.ink_route` = "converted": the Canon IJ and Epson drivers, Gutenprint in its RGB colour model, the sample "RGB" drivers). After such a job the status line says the headline instead of "The printing system confirms …". {printer} is the printer's name as macOS shows it, {inks} the chart's inks in words ("CMYK, 4 inks", "CMY + Orange, 4 inks"). Until approved nothing is asked and the status line after such a job reads "Print job submitted successfully."*

> **macOS converts this chart’s colours**
>
> The driver of {printer} takes RGB, not ink values. macOS therefore turns the chart’s ink values ({inks}) into RGB colours on the way, and the driver works out its own ink amounts from those. The sheet would not carry the chart’s values, and a measurement of it would not describe your printer’s inks.
>
> Print this chart on a printer whose driver takes these inks, or through a RIP that does.


### M-PRINT-INKS-APPROXIMATE · APPROVED · the direct route, a chart of inks other than CMYK or CMY on a PostScript or CMYK raster queue, 4.3.5 B2

*Basti approved this on 2026-10-11 IF every statement is true. The combined review of 4.3.5 (report folder `2026-10-11_435_combined_review`) found one that is not: "prints {extra} as an approximate mix of cyan, magenta, yellow and black". The alternate ChromIQ writes for a DeviceN chart (`PostScriptGenerator._devicen_tint`, the weights in `_INK_TO_CMYK`) gives White no cyan, magenta, yellow or black at all, and Medium Yellow and Medium Black (Add/Remove Colorant 17 and 18) have no weights, so a printer without those inks prints nothing for them. Corrected below, PROPOSED again and not asked. The proposed sentence, for the record:* "One without them, which includes every printer whose driver takes CMYK, prints {extra} as an approximate mix of cyan, magenta, yellow and black on top of the other inks."


*New 2026-10-10 (4.3.5 B2). Basti asked to be told "when DeviceN reaches a printer that cannot honour it (falls back to the approximate CMYK tint transform)". Since B2 a chart whose inks are not CMYK or CMY (CMY + orange, CMYK + orange + green, light inks) goes as DeviceN with its inks named, never as CMYK. A PostScript printer or RIP with inks of those names prints them; any other takes the alternate, ChromIQ's approximate CMYK mix, and a CMYK raster driver always does. Asked like M-PRINT-INKS-CONVERTED, on a PostScript queue and on a CMYK raster queue (`ppd_color.ink_route` = "approximate"); {extra} is the inks past CMYK or CMY ("Orange", "Orange, Green"). Until approved nothing is asked and the status line after such a job reads "Print job submitted successfully."*

> **The chart’s extra inks may be printed as a mix**
>
> The chart has {inks}. ChromIQ sends it to {printer} with every ink named, and a printer or RIP that has inks of those names prints it as it is. One without them, which includes every printer whose driver takes CMYK, does not print {extra} as such: it puts an approximate mix of cyan, magenta, yellow and black in its place on top of the other inks, or, for an ink with no such mix (white among them), nothing at all. Patches with {extra} would then not carry the chart’s values, and a measurement of them would not describe your printer’s inks.

### M-HELP-GAMUT-SIZE-SPREAD · APPROVED · two paragraphs of the "How many colours to test" help — Create Chart, FROM PROFILE GAMUT (k82, 4.3.5)

*Basti approved this on 2026-10-11 as proposed. The combined review of 4.3.5 (report folder `2026-10-11_435_combined_review`) found one statement untrue: "at least eight of them". The grey steps are capped at about one patch in eight with a floor of six (`gamut_target._neutral_budget`), so a chart of 50 to 59 colours (the box allows 50 and up) gets six or seven: measured with Knut's run 5 profile, 55 and 59 colours gave seven steps, 60, 64, 100 and 400 gave eight, 1 000 gave ten, 2 000 thirteen. Everything else held: 400 and 1 000 colours share 193 of the 400, the eight corners are added to every count, and two runs of every count chose the same colours. Corrected below (the second paragraph), PROPOSED again and not shown. The proposed sentence, for the record:* "evenly spaced grey steps run along the neutral axis from the black to the white corner, at least eight of them and never more than about one patch in eight."


*New 2026-10-11, 4.3.5 (k82, Knut #182 6102031563). Since the chart's colours are spread evenly over the profile's gamut for each count, two paragraphs of the count's help stopped being true: "Smaller checks stay comparable with larger ones: every colour of a 400-colour chart is also part of a 1 000-colour chart…" and "Greys have a fixed share: about one patch in eight…". They are left out of the help until these replacements are approved; the rest of the help is unchanged. Shown in the ⓘ of "Colours to test" (`tab_chart._gamut_size_help_body`), the first after the "A guide from practice" paragraph, the second after the "Auto" paragraph.*

> **How many colours to test**
>
> **Each chart is spread for its own size:** the colours are spread evenly over everything your profile can print, so a 400-colour chart and a 1 000-colour chart made from the same profile do not share all their colours. Compare figures from charts of the same size. The eight cube corners are always added on top, whatever you choose here.
>
> **Grey steps:** evenly spaced grey steps run along the neutral axis from the black to the white corner, at least eight of them on a chart of 60 colours or more (six or seven on a smaller one) and never more than about one patch in eight. A change in the printer shows in the greys first. All other colours are spread evenly through the whole range your profile can print: the more colours you choose, the closer together they sit, and none sits closer to another than it needs to.

> **How was this run’s profiling chart printed?**
>
> This run’s profiling chart was printed before ChromIQ 4.3.5. Those versions did not record how a chart was sent to the printer, so ChromIQ cannot tell which way it went. A verification chart only gives a fair result if it goes to the printer the same way as the profiling chart did.
>
> •  If you printed it with ChromIQ’s own printing (“Use default macOS printer dialog” switched off in Preferences), everything is fine. Choose “Print anyway”.
> •  If you printed it through the macOS print dialog, the printer adjusted its colours on the way. Choose “Use the print dialog” to print this verification chart the same way, letting the printer adjust the colours as Preview does, as it did for the profile. Or print and measure the profiling chart again with this version of ChromIQ, and build its profile again, before you verify it.

> **How a PostScript printer gets the chart**
>
> Choose the way you print your photos. A profile only fits photos that reach the printer the same way as its chart did. This printer can receive the chart in two ways, and ChromIQ uses the one you choose here for this run and all its verification charts.
>
> Photoshop (Photoshop Manages Colors): choose this if you print from Photoshop with “Photoshop Manages Colors” and this profile as the printer profile. The chart’s values go to the printer unchanged. (Sent as the printer’s own RGB, like ChromIQ’s direct route.)
>
> Preview and most other apps: choose this if you print from Preview or another app that leaves printing to macOS. The printer then adjusts the colours with its own settings, the same way for the chart and for your photos. To print a photo with this profile from Photoshop in this way: Edit > Convert to Profile (this profile), then Edit > Assign Profile > Don’t Color Manage, and print with “Printer Manages Colors”. (macOS sends the values marked as sRGB, or with the profile set in ColorSync Utility; this only works while no profile is set there.)
>
> If the print dialog has an RGB colour setting for the printer (on an HP Color LaserJet, “RGB Color”), ChromIQ sets it to Device. Do the same for your photos.

The answer is stored for the project (`project.json`), so the calibration, every run and their verification charts are not asked again. Never shown for any other printer. {printer} is the printer's name as macOS shows it. Before the approval nobody was asked and every run printed the default form, as in 4.3.5 beta 1.*

### M-CAL-DONE-UNDERLAY · APPROVED · lay the chart on a white surface, for an instrument with no reading board — Measure, Calibration Complete

*Approved by: Basti, 2026-10-13 ("the underlay text WAS ok"), the combined review's wording below, and switched on. Checked: shown only for a ColorMunki / i1Studio and a CR30 (`ti2_loader.underlay_tip_html`, by `instrument_family`), never for an i1Pro, a SpectroScan or an unknown instrument.*

*New 2026-10-13, 4.3.5 beta 2. Knut, [6123470301](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6123470301): "When using instruments like the CR30 or Colormunki/i1Studio we, as the developer of the app, have no control over the underlying surface a user has when profiling a chart. For the i1Pro series of products, the reader board/jig is designed intentionally with a white color that will not influence reading of charts, but for the other instruments that do not have a reader board the user might just use whatever table surface they have and not think about it, that profiling thinner papers, like 80 to 100 gram plain papers, may be influenced by the color of the underlying surface. The help text for measuring in the help card "Build my First ICC Profile" already addresses this, but the tips/steps described in the Calibration Completed message after calibrating, after starting a measurement, should also mention this detail, for these two instruments mentioned." It is one paragraph with its headline in bold, under the instrument's own steps, in every Calibration Complete window of a ColorMunki / i1Studio or a CR30 (How to Measure, patch by patch or strip by strip, Guided Refinement Ready, Manual Re-measurement) and in the CR30's M-CR30-HOW-TO-MEASURE window. Never for an i1Pro (its reading board is white by design), a SpectroScan or an unknown instrument, and not in M-CAL-REQUESTED-DONE, which only says to carry on. Its advice is the "Build my first ICC profile" card's note "Why the backing has to be white".*

*Rewritten 2026-10-13 (Basti: the friendly style of the cards, what to do first, then why), approved as rewritten. Was: "**What lies under the chart** This instrument has no reading board, so what lies under the chart is up to you. On thin paper, such as 80 to 100 g/m² plain paper, the colour of the table or desk mat shows through and changes every reading, and the profile takes that change on. Lay the chart on a white, even surface that nothing shows through, such as a stack of white paper or of the same paper as the chart."*

> **Lay the chart on a white surface**
>
> Before you measure, lay the chart on a white, even surface that nothing shows through, such as a stack of white paper or of the same paper as the chart. This instrument has no reading board of its own, so what lies under the chart is up to you. On thin paper, such as 80 to 100 g/m² plain paper, the colour of the table or desk mat shows through. It then changes every reading, and the profile takes that change on.

"it" that means a reading, a value or a range is left as it was ("So it is probably not a misread", "it is real, keep it for the profile"). Switched on in 4.3.5 beta 3: the card now shows these lines in place of the texts they replace (listed below), in English and all 13 translations.*

*Proposed 2026-10-12. Knut, [6108217111](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6108217111): "This text is very confusing. Are you saying that the reading before was 6.70 and now confirmed as dE*ab 8.07? Then you say 'Red before: dE 6.44 ...' What do you mean? ... Also, which unit is 6.70, it is dE or dE\*ab? All the hover-text messages for the patch error test and neighbour limit check must be reworded in an understandable text that clearly explains what is meant and what is seen." The words are ours and wait here; **while this message is not approved the card shows the approved texts unchanged** (M-PATCH-NEIGHBOUR, M-PATCH-NEIGHBOUR-VARIANTS, M-PATCH-LIMIT, M-PATCH-CORRECTED and its variants, M-PATCH-UNSETTLED, and the card's own "ΔE\*ab 8.07, the reading before 6.70"). Approved, it replaces them line for line. One term carries the card: a patch's **colour error** is the ΔE\*ab (CIE76, L\*a\*b\* D50) between its reading and its expected colour, the figure the patch error limit is compared with; the neighbour check compares that colour error with the median colour error of the 2 to 4 patches nearest in expected colour. Line 1 replaces the colour section's "ΔE\*ab 8.07 / (CIE76, L\*a\*b\* D50)" and line 2 is new: the same difference in ΔE00, the formula the Measurement Report uses, so a card can be found in the report (the report's own reference is the chart's design; on a verification chart From Profile Gamut it differs from the profile's prediction by 0.01 on most patches, up to ΔE\*ab 3 at the edge of the gamut). Lines 3 to 6 replace M-PATCH-NEIGHBOUR lines 3 to 5 and M-PATCH-NEIGHBOUR-VARIANTS line 2; line 7 the red card's headline sentence (M-PATCH-NEIGHBOUR line 1); line 8 M-PATCH-NEIGHBOUR-VARIANTS line 1; line 9 the yellow card's "Red before: …" (M-PATCH-NEIGHBOUR line 6), which named the neighbour check's verdict on the current reading as if it were history: it says instead what the outline would be without the re-read. Lines 10 to 12 replace M-PATCH-LIMIT's headline and lines 1 and 2 ("reached" becomes "is above": a value on the limit has not been red since 4.3.4); line 13 the yellow card's limit line. Line 14 replaces "ΔE\*ab {de}, the reading before {prev}" (the earlier reading is the one the re-read agreed with). Lines 15 to 18 replace M-PATCH-UNSETTLED lines 1 to 5, line 15 with one earlier reading and line 16 with more. Lines 19 and 20 replace M-PATCH-CORRECTED line 1 and 2 and M-PATCH-CORRECTED-VARIANTS line 1. The headlines "Yellow outline: confirmed by a re-read", "Red outline: the readings do not agree", "Green outline: corrected by a re-read", "Probably a misread: read it again.", the re-read lines and every other line of the cards are unchanged. Placeholders: {de}, {prev}, {own}, {median}, {d}, {limit}, {de00} with two decimals, the figures the tests compare; {kind} one of M-PATCH-LIMIT's chart-type phrases; {n} 2 to 4 (lines 3 to 9), or the number of readings, 3 or more (line 18); {prevs} the earlier readings' colour errors, joined by ", ". Whole sentences: the card wraps them to its width.*

*Revised 2026-10-13 (Basti: "correct but too technical"): every line leads with what it means in plain words, then the numbers, one thought per sentence, the technical names (ΔE\*ab, ΔE00, median, the tests' names, the same-reading tolerance) in brackets at the end, and what it means for the user ("probably not a misread", "not clear yet which one is right"). Two statements of the first wording were not true on every card and are corrected: lines 9 and 13 said "Without the re-read" also on yellow cards confirmed by similar patches or judged like a patch of their colour range, where nothing was read again (they now say "Without that confirmation", and the headline above names it); and line 2 no longer suggests the report shows the card's figure, because the report compares a From Profile Gamut chart with the chart's design, which differs from the profile's prediction by up to ΔE\*ab 2.96 near the gamut's edge on Knut's run 2 chart. Line 10's headline is "Red outline: too far off its expected colour". Placeholders unchanged.*

The units are defined once per card, at the bottom above "See Preferences ▸ Measurement" (the last two lines below), and the bracketed definitions are gone from the lines. The difference between the expected and the measured colour belongs to the pair, so it is no longer a line under "Measured": it is a section of its own after both colours, under the bold heading of line 1, with both formulas on one line the card builds ("ΔE\*ab 8.07   ΔE00 6.46"), what the expected colour is based on (lines 2 to 4, by where it came from: the run profile's prediction on a verification ChromIQ printed, the pre-conditioning profile's prediction on a chart made with one, otherwise the chart's RGB read as sRGB) and the Measurement Report's formula (line 5); it is shown in every view mode. The outlines' headlines are drawn bold, so none reads as a sentence running on into the next line. A card taller than the screen allows is laid out wider instead, in two columns if it must, over the panel beside the chart if it must (the size rule, `ui.tiff_preview.card_limits`), which is layout, not wording, and applies to every card now.*

Lines 15 to 18 counted every reading of the patch, while the code counts only the earlier readings that were red and past the patch error limit (`patch_flags`, `unsettled`): "was {prevs} off at the earlier reading", "The two readings", "You have read this patch {n} times" and "agrees with none of the earlier ones" were untrue for a patch with an earlier reading under the limit; they now say only what is counted. Line 6 lost "yet": the line is also shown on a chart read to the end. The other sixteen lines were checked against `tiff_preview.PatchInfoCard`, `neighbour_check` (Knut's four steps), `patch_flags` and `misread_settings.above` and hold.*

> **Patch error limit and neighbour check on the patch card, in plain words**
>
> Difference between the two colours
> The expected colour is what the run's profile predicts for the values sent to the printer.
> The expected colour is what the profile this chart was made with predicts for this patch.
> The expected colour is an estimate: the patch's RGB values read as sRGB.
> The Measurement Report uses ΔE00. It is closer to how the eye sees colour differences.
> The {n} patches most similar to patch {loc} are about {median} off their expected colours. At {own}, this one stands out by {d}. (Neighbour check, median of the {n}.)
> The {n} patches most similar to patch {loc} are about {median} off their expected colours. At {own}, this one is {d} closer to its expected colour than they are. (Neighbour check, median of the {n}.)
> The {n} patches most similar to patch {loc} are about as far off their expected colours as this one, at {own}. Patch {loc} does not stand out from them. (Neighbour check, median of the {n}.)
> Not compared with similar patches: fewer than 2 patches with a similar expected colour have been read. (Neighbour check, colour-neighbour radius.)
> Red outline: patch {loc} stands out by {d} from the patches most similar in colour. That is more than the neighbour limit of {limit} for {kind}. (Neighbour check.)
> Patch {loc} also stands out by {d} from the patches most similar in colour. That is more than the neighbour limit of {limit} for {kind}. (Neighbour check.)
> Without that confirmation, patch {loc} would be red for standing out by {d} from the patches most similar in colour, more than the neighbour limit of {limit} for {kind}. (Neighbour check.)
> Red outline: too far off its expected colour
> This patch is {de} off its expected colour. That is more than the patch error limit of {limit} for {kind}.
> This patch is {de} off its expected colour. That is more than the patch error limit of {limit} for {kind}. Patch {loc} also stands out from the other patches of its strip. (Strip test.)
> Without that confirmation, patch {loc} would be red for being {de} off its expected colour, more than the patch error limit of {limit} for {kind}.
> You read this patch again, and the new reading agrees with an earlier one. So it is probably not a misread. Patch {loc} is {de} off its expected colour now, and was {prev} off at that earlier reading. (The two readings are within the same-reading tolerance.)
> Patch {loc} is {de} off its expected colour now. An earlier reading was {prevs} off.
> Patch {loc} is {de} off its expected colour now. Earlier readings were {prevs} off.
> This reading and an earlier one are both further off than the patch error limit of {limit} for {kind}, and they do not agree with each other. So it is not clear yet which one is right. (They differ by more than the same-reading tolerance.)
> {n} readings of this patch are further off than the patch error limit of {limit} for {kind}, and this one agrees with none of the others. So it is not clear yet which one is right. (Same-reading tolerance.)
> The earlier, red reading was {de} off its expected colour and stood out from the patches most similar to patch {loc}. The new reading does not stand out more than the neighbour limit allows. (Neighbour check.)
> The earlier, red reading was {de} off its expected colour, more than the patch error limit. The new reading is within the limit.
> ΔE00 = CIEDE2000, L*a*b* D50
> ΔE*ab = CIE76, L*a*b* D50

### M-HELP-COLOUR-VIEW-SEAMS · APPROVED · the 3D tool's “Show:” help, the lines named as seams, 4.3.5 beta 3

*Approved by: Knut, 2026-10-13, #182 [6152691121](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6152691121): "All messages/descriptions are accepted". Shown since then as the tooltip of “Show:” in place of the beta 2 text.*

*New 2026-10-13 (Knut, #182 6144104040: why do the dark lines not align with the outer edges of the grey shell?). The beta 2 tooltip said the lines and the skin are “the edges and sides of everything the profile can print”; the lines are the RGB cube's twelve edges carried through the profile, seams ON the skin. Measured on his CLJ5550 run 2 profile: for 17 of 24 hue sectors the most colourful colour lies inside a face, not on an edge (green at G=53), and the skin reaches up to 38.9 ΔE*ab beyond the lines (dark violet, L* 20 to 30); ET-8550 and a small plain-paper gamut 18 and 18 of 82 and 69 bins at 3 ΔE or more. The tooltip of “Show:” (`patch_cube_dialog._view_help`); hidden until approved, the beta 2 text stays meanwhile. The headline is not shown.*

> **Ink amounts or colours**
>
> Ink amounts: each patch sits at the red, green and blue values the printer is asked for, from 0 to 100.
>
> Colours through the profile: each patch sits where the profile says it lands as a colour (L* up, a* and b* across). The grey skin is everything the profile can print. The darker lines are seams on that skin, not its outline: they are the colours where two of the three ink amounts are at 0 or 100, for example from pure red to pure yellow. On many printers the most colourful colours lie on these seams. On others, often laser printers, the most colourful colours come from other mixes, and the skin bulges out between the seams. The outline you see is simply where the skin turns away from you, so it changes as you turn the view.
>
> The patches stay about half a spacing inside the skin. That is how evenly spaced patches fill a shape: each one stands for the colours around it, so the outermost ones sit a little in from the edge.
>
> A chart made From Profile Gamut spaces its colours evenly as colours. A printer does not respond evenly to ink amounts, so the same chart can look crowded in one part of the RGB cube and sparse in another.

>
> Grey skin: every colour this profile can print (its gamut).
> Lines: seams on the skin, where two of the three inks are at 0 or 100 (for example from pure red to pure yellow). They are not the skin's outline.
> Dots: the chart's patches, each in its own colour.


### M-CHART-STRIP-LABELS-CROWDED · APPROVED · strip letters that run into each other, Create Chart, 4.3.5 beta 3

*Approved by: Knut, 2026-10-13, #182 [6152691121](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6152691121): "All messages/descriptions are accepted". Shown since then in red under “Measured from Preview”.*

*New 2026-10-13 (Knut, #182 6144104040: with many strips the double-letter labels “crash” at a fixed 12 pt; “auto” works; asked for a warning like the text-overlap ones). Shown in red under “Measured from Preview” beside the other overlap notices (`tab_chart._engine_text_notes`), only for a size the user typed and only when a smaller size clears it. Detection: `raster.strip_label_crowding`, with the renderer's font, size and letter spacing on the chart's own labels and strip pitch: neighbours closer than the gap between the letters of one label. Measured on his run 2 layout (A4, By columns / rows, 20 rows): 24 strips at 12 pt clear; 30 strips 0.07 mm apart (fits at 10 pt); 40 strips overlap by 1.35 mm (fits at 8 pt); 40 strips on auto clear. Hidden until approved (`tab_chart.strip_label_crowding_notice`). The headline is not shown.*

> **The strip letters run into each other**
>
> ⚠ The strip letters run into each other. At {size} pt each label is wider than the room above its strip ({pitch} mm from one strip to the next), so neighbours such as “{first}” and “{second}” touch or overlap and are hard to tell apart when you read the chart. In the “Strip & row labels” frame, choose a smaller size next to “Font:” ({fits} pt or smaller fits), or choose “auto”, which picks the largest size that fits by itself.

Many people can not know what photoshop or other software does.”). In place of M-PRINT-PS-ASK once approved, with M-PRINT-PS-FORM-CHOICE-EXPLAINED as its two buttons (the buttons then carry no “Print like”). Each choice by what happens to the colours and when to choose it; Photoshop and Preview only as examples. Checked: “Send the colours unchanged” is D1 (DeviceRGB, the chart's values, the direct route's form, M-PRINT-JOB-DEVICE-RGB); “Let the printer adjust” is the print view as 4.3.4 (CIEBasedABC sRGB, or CIEBasedDEF from the queue's ColorSync profile), measured again on capture queues in this round; “the usual way to make a printer profile”: ArgyllCMS, X-Rite i1Profiler (colour management off for the chart). > **How should ChromIQ send the chart to {printer}?**
>
> {printer} is a PostScript printer, and macOS can hand it the chart in two ways. Choose the way you will later print your photos: a profile only fits pictures that reach the printer exactly the way its chart did. ChromIQ keeps the choice for this whole project, for its calibration, its runs and their verification charts.
>
> Send the colours unchanged: the printer gets the chart’s colour values exactly as ChromIQ made them, and nothing on the way changes them. Choose this when the program you print your photos from converts them with your profile itself before printing (for example Photoshop with “Photoshop Manages Colors” and this profile as the printer profile). ChromIQ also prints this way when you print without the macOS print dialog.
>
> Let the printer adjust the colours: macOS marks the chart as ordinary screen colours (sRGB, or the profile set for this printer in ColorSync Utility), and the printer then changes them with its own colour settings, as it does for most things you print. Choose this when you print from programs that leave the colours to macOS and the printer (for example Preview). The profile then describes your printer together with that adjustment, and fits only photos printed the same way.
>
> Not sure? Choose “Send the colours unchanged”. It is the usual way to make a printer profile, because nothing between ChromIQ and the paper changes the colours.

### M-PRINT-DIALOG-COLOUR-MATCHING · APPROVED · why the macOS print dialog shows a colour profile, 4.3.5 beta 3

*Approved by: Knut, 2026-10-13, #182 [6152691121](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6152691121): "All messages/descriptions are accepted". Shown since then as a paragraph of the dialog route's notice.*

*New 2026-10-13 (Knut, #182 6144104040: the dialog shows his default profile under Colour Matching, ColorSync or “In printer”, on the Bonjour and the PostScript driver, and it cannot be switched off; the tab must explain it). Measured on capture queues (report folder `2026-10-13_b3_knut/item3`, never a printer): a generic PostScript queue and the HP Color LaserJet 5550 PPD with his run 5 profile set in ColorSync Utility (the dialog then shows ColorSync and that profile), both PostScript forms, a profiling and a From Profile Gamut chart, and the Canon PRO-300 driver: the job with ColorSync left as shown and the job with “In printer” (Canon: its own matching) chosen are byte for byte the same after the volatile fields (date, title, job number) are masked, 10 pairs; the chart's pixels reach the printer unchanged (DeviceRGB) or as the chosen PostScript form says (CIEBasedABC/DEF). The reason: ChromIQ locks application colour matching (`native_print_macos._LOCKED_COLOR_SETTINGS`), as Photoshop does; X-Rite documents the same for i1Profiler (ColorSync shown pre-selected but bypassed). A paragraph of the dialog route's notice after “ChromIQ asks for application colour matching…” (`tab_print._macos_dialog_notice`); the headline is not shown. Hidden until approved.*

> **Why the print dialog shows a colour profile**
>
> In the print dialog, under Colour Matching, macOS may show “ColorSync” with a profile already chosen (often your default profile), and it offers no way to switch colour matching off. You can leave it as it is. ChromIQ tells macOS that it manages the chart’s colours itself, the same way Photoshop does with “Photoshop Manages Colors”, so this setting is not applied to the chart. Measured: with “ColorSync” and a profile, or with “In printer”, the printer received exactly the same job. How the chart’s colours reach the printer is decided by ChromIQ, by the settings on this tab.

### M-PRINT-PS-FORM-HELP-PROJECT-EXPLAINED · APPROVED · the help of the PostScript row, the project rule and each choice explained, 4.3.5 beta 4

*Approved by: Knut, 2026-10-13, #182 [6152691121](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6152691121): "All messages/descriptions are accepted" (text 6 of the post: "the help of that row, and the line under it, in the same words. The first paragraph says that the choice belongs to the project, as the question above does"). It merges two proposals, which it supersedes (below): the first paragraph of M-PRINT-PS-FORM-HELP-PROJECT (the project rule) and the explained paragraphs of M-PRINT-PS-FORM-HELP-EXPLAINED. The ⓘ beside M-PRINT-PS-FORM-CHOICE-EXPLAINED, in place of M-PRINT-PS-FORM-HELP-TITLE (`tab_print.ps_texts`). Shown since 4.3.5 beta 4.*

> **Choose the way you print your photos**
>
> A profile only fits photos that reach the printer the same way as its chart did. This printer can receive the chart in two ways. The way chosen at the project’s first print to a PostScript printer through the macOS print dialog is kept for the whole project: its calibration, its runs and their verification charts. A choice made here applies to this run and its verification charts, and to runs refined from it that have no choice of their own. The project’s choice stays as it is.
>
> Send the colours unchanged: the printer gets the chart’s colour values exactly as ChromIQ made them, and nothing on the way changes them. Choose this when the program you print your photos from converts them with your profile itself before printing (for example Photoshop with “Photoshop Manages Colors” and this profile as the printer profile).
>
> Let the printer adjust the colours: macOS marks the chart as ordinary screen colours (sRGB, or the profile set for this printer in ColorSync Utility), and the printer then changes them with its own colour settings, as it does for most things you print. Choose this when you print from programs that leave the colours to macOS and the printer (for example Preview). The profile then describes your printer together with that adjustment, and fits only photos printed the same way. To print a photo with this profile from Photoshop in this way: Edit > Convert to Profile (this profile), then Edit > Assign Profile > Don’t Color Manage, and print with “Printer Manages Colors”. This only works while no profile is set for the printer in ColorSync Utility.
>
> If the print dialog has an RGB colour setting for the printer (on an HP Color LaserJet, “RGB Color”), ChromIQ sets it to Device. Do the same for your photos.

### M-ALL-STRIPS-PATCHES-LEFT · APPROVED (revised 2026-08-14, headline 2026-10-14) · every strip read, but patches inside them are not — Measure tab

**Approved by:** Knut, 2026-10-15 ([#182 6181524471](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6181524471), "All the messages are otherwise approved", the beta 5 texts of [6176326618](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6176326618)).

> **All strips are read, but some patches are not**
>
> Every strip has been read, but {n} patches still have no reading. Everything you have read so far is safe.
>
> This usually happens when some patches were read one at a time in **Patch-by-patch mode** and a few were stepped over.
>
> To finish them, start measuring again with **Patch-by-patch mode** ticked and **Refine / resume existing measurement (-r)** ticked. ChromIQ picks up where the readings stop, so you only measure the patches that are still missing rather than the whole chart again.
>
> • **Re-read Individual Strips**: stay in this session and read a strip again now. Use **f** and **b** to move between strips, **n** to jump to the next unread one, and **d** when you are done.
>
> • **Close**: finish here. ChromIQ asks whether to keep what you have measured so far, so nothing is decided behind your back.

*With one patch left the headline is* **All strips are read, but one patch is not**.

*Punctuation only, after the approval (4.3.5 beta 7, CLAUDE.md's em dash rule): the two bullets took a colon after the button's name in place of the em dash, as the other windows' button bullets have it, in English and in all 13 languages. No word changed.*

*Headline revised 2026-10-14 (4.3.5 beta 5 regression review), wording only.
It read "Some patches are still unread", one word away from the approved
navigation question M-UNREAD-NEXT-OR-JUMP-STRIP / -PATCH ("Some patches are
still not read"), which can open in the same session and asks something else:
where the reader goes next, while this one stands in for "All Strips Read".
They are different situations, so this window keeps its own and its headline
now says how it differs. When it opens changed too (behaviour, awaiting
confirmation): on a resume whose every strip already counted as read when the
session opened, the first strip read again made the engine report the chart
complete, and this window came straight after Calibration Complete. There it
now waits until the session has read every strip; where a strip was still
unread at the start, reading the last one brings it, as before
(`MeasureManager.patches_left_is_news`).*

*Revised after Knut's review of the first draft (2026-08-14), which he corrected
on three counts.*

**1. The cause was wrong.** The first draft said *"a slight wobble as the
instrument passes over them is enough"*. His answer: *"is not likely. if not
enough patches are registered it is caught. The likely reason is that a user has
used patch-by-patch mode to read some patches and missed some."* The message now
says that instead. Nothing here asserts a mechanism that has not been observed.

**2. The button was invented.** The first draft told the user to press
**"Stop & Save"**, which is not a button this app has. His answer: *"The button
'Stop & Save' is not the wording used for other windows … like the All Patches
Read (for patch-by-patch mode) and All Strips Read (for strip mode) [which] have
one button to Close, which calls the window where user decides to stop and save,
or stop and discard. This is the unified exit method defined in the design spec,
which you would have known."* He is right that it is defined, and right that I
should have read it: `measurement_exit_strategy.md` §"The single exit".

**3. Every button needs its own explanation** — *"the rules used in the design
specification is that all windows have an explanation for each button in a
window"* — so both now carry one.

**It must exist in all four cases.** Strip mode and patch-by-patch, on ChromIQ's
engine and on stock ArgyllCMS chartread, are four separate windows with different
exit keys behind the same buttons (`measurement_exit_strategy.md`, Tables 1 and
2). A window raised from one parser only reaches half the users, and the stock
half working is what has hidden that four times already. So this window is to be
raised from code both `_handle_line` and `_handle_engine_line` reach, and its
Close must delegate to `_confirm_end_of_session`, which already knows which mode
and which reader it is in rather than sending a key of its own.

**4. It is a STRIP-MODE window, so its button re-reads strips.** The first
revision offered "Re-read Patches", which he corrected: *"this message is for a
strip mode session (and this message only happens during strip mode), not a
patch-by-patch session. Here one would 'Re-read strips'."* The button now matches
the completion window it stands in for, and the guidance in the body still points
at patch-by-patch + resume, because that is how the missing patches get finished
in a later session — which he approved separately.

**Close — ruled 2026-08-14.** He answered **(A)**: *"Close should raise the 'Keep
what you have measured so far?' window. However, the description 'keeps the
measurement, goes nowhere' is still correct, because it is referring to the other
button that says to jump to build profile tab."* So the row in
`measurement_exit_strategy.md` is not stale — it was read against the wrong
button. Close raises the ending; the Go-to-tab button is the one that keeps the
measurement and moves on.

**Both readers, per his instruction:** *"If this check is possible to implement
for the stock argyllcms chartread engine also, then the button commands should be
made to use the correct command for the specific chartread engine, according to
the measurement exit strategy in the design specification. Use the All Strips
Read window for each engine as basis for the correct action to use to re-read or
to Close / exit."* So both buttons take their keys from the All Strips Read row
of Table 1 (engine) and Table 2 (stock) rather than sending anything of their
own.

> **PostScript printers: choose how you print your photos**
>
> Many colour laser printers are PostScript printers: they take the page in a printer language called PostScript. Through the macOS print dialog they can receive the chart in two ways. Choose the way you print your photos. ChromIQ asks after you click Print in the print dialog, the first time a chart of this project goes to a PostScript printer, and keeps your answer for the whole project: its calibration, its runs and their verification charts. The “{print_like}” row on the Print Chart tab then shows the choice, and a change made there applies to that run and its verification charts only.
> • “{photoshop}”: choose this if you print from Photoshop with “Photoshop Manages Colors” and this profile as the printer profile. The chart's values go to the printer unchanged.
> • “{preview}”: choose this if you print from Preview or another app that leaves printing to macOS. The printer then adjusts the colours with its own settings, the same way for the chart and for your photos.
>
> A run you refine from another one starts with that run's choice. Sent straight to the printer, without the dialog, the chart always goes the Photoshop way.
>
> If the print dialog has an RGB colour setting for the printer (on an HP Color LaserJet, “RGB Color”), ChromIQ sets it to Device. Do the same for your photos.

### M-END-WRITTEN · APPROVED · the ending window once ChromIQ's engine has already written the session's readings — Measure tab, 4.3.5 beta 5

**Approved by:** Knut, 2026-10-15 ([#182 6181524471](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6181524471), "All the messages are otherwise approved", the beta 5 texts of [6176326618](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6176326618)).

*New 2026-10-14 (4.3.5 beta 5 regression review). M-END's first sentence, "They are not in your measurement file yet", is true of stock ArgyllCMS chartread, which writes the `.ti3` only on a clean exit (§0), and untrue of ChromIQ's engine, which writes it after every strip (and patch) it accepts; since beta 5 "Discard and stop" takes those readings out again (§2, the awaiting-confirmation block). So once the session has changed the file on disk the window keeps M-END's headline and buttons and shows this body instead. {kept} is M-END's approved sentence, "Your previous measurement of {m} patches is put back exactly as it was." (with its paragraph break), when a measurement was there before, including one "Measure anyway" moved to `old/` at Start; otherwise nothing. Shown since 4.3.5 beta 5.*

> **Keep what you have measured so far?**
>
> You have read {n} patches in this session. ChromIQ's engine has already written them into your measurement file.
>
> What each button does:
>
> •  Save and stop: keeps them in this run's measurement file and ends the session. You can carry on later with “Refine / resume existing measurement (-r)”, reading only the strips or patches that are still missing.
>
> •  Discard and stop: ends the session and keeps nothing from it. The file this session wrote is moved to an “old” folder, never deleted.{kept}
>
> •  Keep measuring: closes this window and carries on where you were.

*With one patch read:* "You have read 1 patch in this session. ChromIQ's engine has already written it into your measurement file." and "Save and stop: keeps it in this run's measurement file …", the rest as above.

### M-CONVERT-TOOL-MISSING · APPROVED · the file converter cannot find its ArgyllCMS program — every import and conversion door, 4.3.5 beta 6

**Approved by:** Knut, 2026-10-15 ([#182 6181598560](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6181598560), "Specified messages 1 to 11 ... Approved from my point of view", the texts of [6181127728](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6181127728)).

*New 2026-10-15, after #209. The reporter's screenshot showed a Russian window whose only English paragraph was the reason it opened: `ReferenceConvertError` (`workflow/reference_convert.py`) carried hard-coded English text into every window that shows it, and no translation could reach it. Each of the converter's reasons is now a message here, M-CONVERT-*, rendered in the user's language when it is raised (the language is fixed for the session, and `core.i18n` needs no Qt), and the exception carries the message's ID and headline. They all share one headline, the one the Measure tab's import and Build Profile's "Load measurement data" already show for a failed conversion. Where they appear: the Measure tab's IMPORT module (profiling and verification runs), Build Profile's "Load measurement data" and its calibration loader (Run type = Calibration), the Measurement Report's "Add Profile's Measurements", Tools > Convert i1Profiler (its log), and the scanner windows (their note and log). `{tool}` is the program's file name as it is in the ArgyllCMS folder (`txt2ti3.exe` on Windows); `{detail}` is the program's own last line, left as it wrote it; `{name}` is the file's name. Wording ours; shown since 4.3.5 beta 6.*

> **The file could not be converted**
>
> ChromIQ converts this file with a program that comes with ArgyllCMS ({tool}), and that program is not in the ArgyllCMS folder ChromIQ is set to use.
>
> Open Preferences (⚙) and check the ArgyllCMS folder: it should be the “bin” folder inside your ArgyllCMS installation. Then try again.
>
> Your file has not been changed.

### M-ENGINE-FELL-BACK · APPROVED (revised 2026-10-15) · ChromIQ's own measuring engine could not use the instrument — Measure tab

**Approved by:** Knut, 2026-10-15 ([#182 6191537939](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6191537939), *"Regarding "Measuring with ArgyllCMS instead": what stops working. Answer: message accepted"*), the revised text below.

> **Measuring with ArgyllCMS instead**
>
> ChromIQ's own measuring engine could not use your instrument this time, so the measurement has been started again using ArgyllCMS's chartread. Carry on measuring as you normally would: nothing you have already read is lost.
>
> Until this measurement ends, these ChromIQ features do not work:
>
> •  ChromIQ's sounds for each reading are silent. The beeps you hear come from ArgyllCMS.
> •  There is no reading speed check.
> •  The preview shows no measured colours, no red, yellow or green outlines (patch error limit and neighbour check) and no values on hover. Patch by patch, it does not highlight the next patch.
> •  “Was a strip read twice?” is not asked.
> •  A patch you read again in this measurement is not marked as confirmed (yellow), even when the reading comes back the same.
> •  After you read a strip or patch again, ChromIQ does not ask whether to carry on with the next one or jump to one that is still unread: ArgyllCMS decides where to go next.
> •  Your readings are saved only when the measurement ends, not after every strip.
> •  A wrong strip or a very unexpected reading is not shown in a window: ArgyllCMS asks about it in the output field below. Answer with the key it names there.
> •  Calibrate (the K key) and clicking a strip or patch in the preview to go to it are not available.
>
> Reason: {reason}

*Revised 2026-10-15 at Knut's request ([#182 6181524471](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6181524471)), shown from 4.3.5 beta 7.* He deleted *"ArgyllCMS makes its own beeps as it reads, and playing ChromIQ's sounds on top would double every one of them."* and asked for the other things that stop working when ArgyllCMS takes over, *"based on actually what happens in the code"*. The list is exactly that; nothing is on it that the code does not show. The em dash of the first paragraph became a colon. Where each point comes from (proved = a driver drove the real Measure tab through the real fallback on screen, 4.3.5 beta 7 builder report `drive_engine_fell_back.py`; code = read in the code only):

| Point | Why, in the code | |
|---|---|---|
| sounds | `SoundManager.play` drops every sound but the completion sounds while `_reading_engine` is False (`core/sound.py`); `TabMeasure._silence_for_stock_chartread` sets it on the fallback. Window cues (`play_window`) still sound | proved (the flag), code (the sound) |
| reading speed | `_report_strip_pace` times from `scan_started` / `scan_ready` and `strip_measured`, which only `MeasureManager._handle_engine_line` emits; the "Strip Read Quickly" window is engine only | proved |
| preview colours, outlines, hover values | `_on_strip_measured` / `_on_patch_measured` (the patch error limit, the neighbour check, the cards) hang on `strip_measured` / `patch_measured`, engine only; so does the closing window's list of suspected misreads | proved |
| next patch highlight | `_on_patch_ready`, engine only; stock chartread's "Ready to read patch" gives a status line | code |
| "Was a strip read twice?" | `strip_read_twice`, engine only (`_read_twice_was_active` asks `engine_active`) | code |
| a re-read confirming a patch (yellow) | `patch_flags.FlagJudge.judge` lets only a live reading confirm (`live=True`); stock chartread hands over no reading until it writes its file, so a strip or patch read twice in the session leaves only its last reading. Added in the review of 4.3.5 beta 7 | code |
| "Continue to next / Jump to unread" | `MeasureManager._after_a_read` returns unless the engine is active (Knut, 5958921500 Q2: *"This function only applies to ChromIQ measurement engine"*); chartread moves on by itself, to the next unread strip, or patch by patch to the next patch (chartread.c 1486, 2421). Added in the review of 4.3.5 beta 7 | code |
| saved after every strip | the engine writes the `.ti3` after every accepted strip (`readings_saved`, the auto-save note); stock chartread writes it on a clean ending only (§0) | proved (no note), code |
| wrong strip, unexpected reading | the windows answer the engine's typed events (`wrong_strip`, `unexpected_response`); the stock parser raises neither window (it reads "very unexpected response" only to count a strip kept there), so chartread's own prompts (chartread.c 1854, 1887) reach the log only, where the user's key is passed on | code |
| Calibrate, click to go | `can_calibrate_on_request` and `_on_preview_strip_clicked` / `_on_preview_patch_clicked` require the live engine | proved |

Not on the list because it still works on stock chartread: the progress percentage (since 4.3.5 beta 7 each strip or patch stock chartread accepts is counted from the chart, `stock_strip_read` / `stock_patch_read`; before, it stayed where the session started, and a fresh chart read whole ended on "N patches still have no reading"), the strip highlight, f / b / n / d, the misread, instrument-error and sensor-position windows, Save and stop, the "Are you sure" question on unread patches, the measurement-finished sound.

*Why it was proposed.* Knut asked for it directly (#148, 2026-08-14): *"there should be a defined and approved instrument error message in the design specification for this error, is there not? I think there should be a warning message so the user knows."* It is shown as a window since 4.3.5 beta 5, after the line in the measurement log (`workflow/measure_manager.py`). It opens on the restart before any reading (`engine_fell_back`); the mid-chart resume (`engine_fell_back_resumed`) still gives a status line only.

### M-CONVERT-NOT-SAVED · APPROVED · the converted calibration measurement could not be saved beside the export — Build Profile, Run type = Calibration, 4.3.5 beta 7

**Approved by:** Knut, 2026-10-15 ([#182 6191537939](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6191537939), *"Message for "The converted measurement could not be saved" approved."*).

*New 2026-10-15. Build Profile's calibration loader converts an i1Profiler export (.txt / .mxf / .cxf, since 4.3.5 beta 6) and saves the result as `<stem>.ti3` beside the export, never over a file (`TabProfile._convert_calibration_measurement`). When that save failed, a read-only folder or a full disk, the window said ChromIQ "could not read" the file as a measurement: it had just read and converted it, so the user was sent to look at a file that was fine. The conversion's own failures keep their M-CONVERT-* messages. {name}: the export's file name; {saved_as}: the name it was to be saved under; {folder}: that folder; {reason}: the system's own words. Wording ours; shown from 4.3.5 beta 7.*

> **The converted measurement could not be saved**
>
> ChromIQ converted {name}, but could not save the result as {saved_as} in this folder:
> {folder}
>
> The folder may be read-only, or the disk may be full.
>
> Your file has not been changed. Copy it to a folder you can save to, for example one in your home folder, and load it from there.
>
> Details: {reason}

## M-PROPOSED. Messages awaiting review

*This section is where a new or revised message goes: add it to
`workflow/measurement_messages.py` with `approved=False`, write it here, and
list it on the issue. `tests/test_message_catalogue.py` holds the two in step —
it fails if a proposed message is missing from this section, and equally if an
approved one is left sitting in it.*

**A PROPOSED MESSAGE IS SHOWN IN THE APP, TRANSLATED, FROM THE BETA THAT
PROPOSES IT.** Knut, 2026-10-14
([#182 6166519230](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6166519230)):
*"You keep hiding changed messages in new releases. This is not the right way
... You must always release the suggested text. We can approve the text after
as usual, and if it is accepted no new beta is required for the sake of the
text."* So "PROPOSED" is the state of the WORDING, never a switch on what the
user sees: no window, card, help, status line or log line waits for approval,
and nothing outside the catalogue reads `approved`
(`tests/test_a_proposed_text_is_shown.py`). A message stays listed here until
it is approved, and moves to §M then; if the approval changes the words, the
next beta carries the new words. Until 4.3.5 beta 4 the rule was the opposite
("not written into a tab until it is approved"), and texts were held back
behind `approved` or spoke only through the log; every such gate was switched
live in 4.3.5 beta 5.

**Approved texts changed at Knut's request** are changed in place in §M, with
the request named under the entry, and stay approved; the exact new wording
waits for his confirmation there (first case: the patch cards' "patch {loc}"
for "it", 4.3.5 beta 5, #182 6167582807, confirmed by Knut 2026-10-15,
#182 6181524471).

### M-PRINT-JOB-NOT-AS-SENT · PROPOSED · a window when the job read back from the printing system does not carry what ChromIQ sent, beta 15

Replaces the beta 14 window "Colour Management Lock Not Verified". {details} is one line per key, "{key}: {got} (ChromIQ sent {want})"; the line "The chart could not be given the job's own profile, so macOS may convert its colours." is added when, besides, the chart on the macOS dialog route could not be given the job's paper profile. When that is the only problem, M-PRINT-JOB-UNTAGGED is shown instead. Sebastian, 2026-10-08, did not approve this wording: "the reviewer said it is wrong. so i probably can't approve this" (the opening sentence was wrong for the untagged case, which now has its own window).*

> **The print job is not what ChromIQ sent**
>

>
> {details}

### M-PRINT-JOB-UNTAGGED · PROPOSED · a window when the chart could not be given the paper profile its job prints with, macOS dialog route, beta 15

*New 2026-10-08 (beta 15 builder round). The macOS dialog route tags the chart with the paper profile the job prints with (the output intent macOS gives it), so the conversion macOS applies is the identity. When that profile could not be read, or the job read back from CUPS prints with another one (compared byte for byte), and nothing else on the job differs, this window says so. Asked for by Sebastian on 2026-10-08: M-PRINT-JOB-NOT-AS-SENT's opening sentence ("other colour settings than ChromIQ asked for") was wrong for this case. The advice names the other route, which tags the chart itself.* **Not shown** after the P18 window's "Use the print dialog" (M-PRINT-VERIFY-PS-EARLIER-ASK), where the user chose to let the printer adjust the colours; the status line then says the job was sent (R3-1, Basti, 2026-10-20).

*⏳ Awaiting confirmation (4.3.5, report folder `2026-10-10_435_B1`). **Confirmed by:** *nobody yet.* Not shown for a CMYK raster job. Basti chose on 2026-10-10, of the options in B5's analysis, to leave the chart untagged on a queue whose driver takes CUPS raster in a CMYK-family colour space, on condition that the detection is accurate: there macOS converts the chart from its own tag and ignores an RGB profile assigned in ColorSync (review R3, B5; a CMYK profile assigned there is used for the conversion, review R1), so the re-tag only made the sheet depend on that profile. The dialog route decides it from the options the job carries after the dialog (`native_print_macos.cmyk_raster_job`, `ppd_color.raster_colour`): CMYK only when every print-data filter of the PPD takes `application/vnd.cups-raster`, every option that sets `cupsColorSpace` resolves for this job (its own value, else the PPD default and any lpoptions value) to a choice the PPD defines, every colour space those choices set is CMY, YMC, CMYK, YMCK, KCMY or KCMYcm, and macOS's own colour space model of the job, when it names one, is CMYK. Anything else (PostScript, PDF, URF or PWG raster, a vendor type, a second route beside the raster one, an RGB, grey, DeviceN or ICC raster space, an option that cannot be resolved) is not CMYK and keeps the re-tag and this window as before. After the job is sent the same decision is made again from the job read back from CUPS; only if that is CMYK raster too does this window stay away, otherwise it is shown as before.*

> **The chart may not print with its own colours**
>
> The job was sent, but ChromIQ could not give the chart the profile this job prints with. macOS may therefore change the chart’s colours on the way to the printer, and a measurement of that sheet would not describe your printer.
>
> If it has not printed yet, cancel it in the printer’s queue and print again. If this message comes back, turn off “Use default macOS printer dialog” in Preferences and print from the Print Chart tab directly.

### M-PRINT-PAPER-PROFILE-UNKNOWN · PROPOSED · the direct route does not know which paper profile the driver of this model chooses, Print Chart tab, beta 15

*New 2026-10-08 (beta 15 builder round). Basti: the direct route sends the paper profile the vendor's own print dialog would choose for the medium. ChromIQ knows it from the installed driver's own table (Canon IJ media database, Epson PDEData.dat), from the tables measured and shipped with it (`data/printer_paper_profiles.json`: PRO-300/310/200S/1000/1100/100, ET-8550/18100, SC-P700/900/5300/800, Stylus Photo R2000/R3000), or from the user's own earlier prints through the macOS dialog (`workflow/printer_memory.py`). For any other Canon IJ or Epson model it must not guess silently: this window comes before the confirmation window. {printer} is the queue, {medium} the paper type as the driver names it, {profile} the driver's standard setting for the paper profile (the PPD's default, which Epson labels "None"), which a job sent anyway carries. Review 2, 2026-10-08: "standard profile (None)" was untrue for an Epson, so the sentence names the setting. The buttons: "Use the macOS Print Dialog" (the default: prints this chart through the dialog, with the printer already chosen), "Print Anyway", "Cancel". A printer with no paper profiles at all (generic, driverless, Xerox, Gutenprint) never sees it: it prints exactly as in beta 14.*

> **ChromIQ does not know this printer’s paper profiles yet**
>
> ChromIQ does not know which paper profile the driver of {printer} chooses for the paper type “{medium}”. A print from Photoshop gets that paper profile from the printer’s own print dialog, and the chart has to print in the same state.
>
> Print this chart through the macOS print dialog and pick the same paper type there. The driver then chooses the paper profile itself, and ChromIQ remembers its choice, so later charts for this printer and paper type can go straight to the printer.
>
> If you print straight to the printer anyway, the chart goes with the driver’s standard setting for the paper profile ({profile}), which may not be what your prints from Photoshop get on this paper.

### M-VERIFY-UNCHECKED-METRICS · PROPOSED · what the report does with a metric the chart cannot answer — the presets window, with one line in the Measure tab pre-flight

*New for 4.3.0-beta.35 (#182). Knut, 2026-09-22: a report that judges metrics
which cannot be calculated carries a warning for each of them, and the reader
should be told, before anything is printed, that those metrics can be switched
off in Report limits by setting the threshold to "-", so that what is handed to
a customer holds only the metrics that were actually checked.*

**⚠ HIS PREMISE WAS MEASURED AND IT HOLDS IN A MINORITY OF STATES. Two
questions are put back to him below; nothing here is settled.** An adversary
round drove every combination in the real app:

* **the limit SET decides whether such a row appears at all.** Only the two
  ISO-derived sets put a real limit on the rows a ChromIQ verification chart
  cannot answer; the five ChromIQ sets put none, so on them the row is simply
  left out. "A report judging metrics that cannot be calculated carries a
  warning for each" describes 2 of the 7 selectable sets. On the other five the
  remedy is also a no-op, because the threshold is already "no limit".
* **the report TYPE decides too.** One run, four buildable types: the numbered
  note exists on T2 alone. T4 is ungraded, so `_note_the_absences` returns
  early and no row carries one; T3 does not carry those rows at all; T1 carries
  no metric rows. The pre-flight cannot know the type (it asks `assess_any`,
  which unions every combination), so anything it says about notes is wrong on
  three of the four.
* **"-" cannot be typed.** One row, both states: typing "-" into the threshold
  box leaves `hasAcceptableInput()` False and the cell silently reverts on
  focus-out, with the old value still stored. The gesture is setting the spin
  box to ZERO, which it displays as "–" through `setSpecialValueText`. The mark
  is an en dash everywhere in the app and his message spelled it as a hyphen.
* **the lever is often absent.** On a locked run every column is read-only,
  photographed on his own demo project with zero spin boxes in the whole table,
  and the two ISO columns are read-only in every state.

*So the text below says what is invariant, names what decides the rest, and
qualifies the instruction instead of promising it works everywhere.*

**⚠ TWO QUESTIONS FOR KNUT, neither answered:** (1) he asked for this in the
pre-flight popup AND in the presets window, and in the same specification he
asked that the popup not *"become too long"*. Measured on screen, appending the
full paragraph took the popup's `minimumHeight()` from 798 px to 958 in English
and 974 in German, on a window with no scroll area, against about 918 px of
usable height on a 13-inch MacBook Air: the OK button and his own "do not show
this again" tick would be off the bottom of the screen. So the popup carries
one line and the window carries the paragraph. (2) Since most sets already
leave these rows out, is the behaviour he wants actually the ISO sets' one, and
should the ISO-derived sets stop showing rows nothing can answer?

**Question (1) ANSWERED, 2026-09-23** ([5795087247](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-5795087247),
*"Leave the window wider as previously specified"*, R2 of 5781645939). From
beta 39 the pre-flight carries the FULL paragraph below, heading and body, in a
box widened to 968 px; measured on screen it is 827 px tall in English and 875
in German. The one line stays, used only where the shown box would not fit the
screen's work area (a 13-inch Air with the Dock at the bottom, about 860 px).
`docs/design/measurement_report_limits.md` §21.3. The WORDING of both is
unchanged and still waits here. Question (2) was answered in the same comment
(the general rule for unanswerable rows) and is not built by this change.

*The pre-flight's one line, appended under its metric list only when the chart
really falls short of something AND the wide box would not fit the screen:*

> A metric this chart cannot answer is never judged and can never make the report fail. Whether it is shown at all is decided by the limit set, and the window named above says how to change that.

*The paragraph, in the right-hand pane of "Which presets can be used for

> **What the report does with a metric this chart cannot answer**
>
> It is never judged, and it can never make the report fail.

Where the set puts a real limit on the metric, the metric is shown reading N-A, and on a report type that carries notes it also carries one saying what it needed. Where the set puts no limit on it, the metric is left out; that is what ChromIQ's own sets do with the metrics above.
>

*Revised 2026-09-23 for beta 38: the paragraph said "row" four times in the one window Knut's beta 25 item 4 cleared of the word; it says "metric" now. Still PROPOSED.*

*Revised for beta 40 (K31, Knut [5801677743](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-5801677743)): the last paragraph said "in the run's limits, where those limits can still be edited". A run holds no limits of its own any more and nothing is locked, so the lever is the report's own column. Still PROPOSED.*

### ⏳ Awaiting confirmation — the log rule no longer describes what CR30 does

**Confirmed by:** *nobody yet.* This is a discrepancy report and a proposed
amendment, not a change to the rule. Nothing here is in force.

§M says that a message whose wording is not yet approved says its piece **in the
log** until it is. For the CR30 messages that is no longer true of any of them:

| message | where its text appears | wording |
|---|---|---|
| M-CR30-CALIBRATE | window | `approved=False` |
| M-CR30-CALIBRATE-BLACK | window | `approved=False` |
| M-CR30-MAGNET | window | `approved=False` |
| M-CR30-INSTRUMENT-GONE | window | `approved=False` |
| M-CR30-READ-FAILED | window | `approved=False` |

Each window exists because **Basti asked for that window**, in his own words,
after meeting the fault himself — the magnet one after a MacBook recalibrated
his instrument mid-chart, the read-failure one after missing a grey line under
the buttons, the instrument-gone one on 2026-08-30: *"if this is an important
message this should be in a pop up windows with benefitial options for this
case"*.

So this is not four exceptions accumulating. It is the rule having stopped
describing practice, which is worse, because the next message will break it
without anyone noticing.

**Proposed amendment, for Basti or Knut to accept or reject:**

> Proposed wording may be shown in a window when the window itself has been
> asked for. The WORDING remains §M-PROPOSED and unapproved either way, and
> still needs review before it can move to §M.

The distinction that matters is preserved: a ruling that a *window* should exist
is not an approval of the *text* inside it. What the log rule was protecting —
that nobody's unreviewed prose quietly becomes the specification — is untouched,
because none of these five is marked approved.

**If this is rejected**, the honest alternative is to put all five back to
log-only, which reverses four decisions Basti made deliberately. Recording it
that way so the choice is visible rather than drifted into.

*Raised by the round-3 review, 2026-08-30.*
