### Button label — the driver consent window's decline button (AGENT-BD) — ⏳ Awaiting confirmation

**Confirmed by:** *nobody yet.* Proposed 2026-09-05 by AGENT-BD. Basti approved
the CHANGE — *"fix the ok button and the grammar, then land it"* — but not a
particular phrase, so the phrase is here for him to correct.

*Deliberately NOT given an `M-` identifier, for the reason the two sections above
give: §M is a catalogue of MESSAGES, each one rendered from
`workflow/measurement_messages.py`, and `tests/test_message_catalogue.py`
requires every `M-` heading in this document to exist there. A button label is
not a message and must not be given a fake identifier to satisfy a parser. It is
recorded here because it is user-facing wording and this is where user-facing
wording is proposed and ruled on.*

`ui/dialogs/settings_dialog.py::_driver_notice` shows two kinds of window. With
no second button it is a NOTICE — it asks nothing, and **OK** is exactly the
right word for acknowledging one. With a second button it is an OFFER, and then
the plain button is the **DECLINE**: `ok.clicked.connect(dlg.reject)`,
deliberately, because `box.accepted` fires for OK too and that is how OK once
came to start an elevated driver install (`f7a565ad`).

The behaviour has been right since that commit and a mutation kills seven tests
if it is undone. **The WORD was still wrong.** On "Before ChromIQ starts" —
the one window in ChromIQ whose entire purpose is informed consent — the row
read `Herunterladen und installieren` and `OK`, and OK is the word most people
read as "yes". Somebody skimming clicks it meaning to agree and gets the
opposite of what they intended, which is the single mistake that window exists
to prevent.

| proposed label | replaces | German | where it appears |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Not now** | OK | Jetzt nicht | the dismissing button of any driver window that OFFERS something |

*It is not new vocabulary. `ui/cr30_calibration.py` already builds a button
labelled **Not now** for exactly this meaning — declining an offered action in a
window that can be opened again — so this reuses that key rather than adding a
thirteenth way to say no, and German is already translated. **Zero new
translation keys.***

*It is correct on all five offers this window makes — `Download and install`,
`Check and install`, `I already have the folder…`, `Choose a different folder…`
and `Try Zadig` — and nothing is lost by pressing it: every one of these windows
is reachable again from Preferences ▸ Instrument drivers…. A label naming the
action ("Don't install") would be correct on two of the five and wrong on three.*

*The alternative considered and not chosen was Qt's **Cancel** / `Abbrechen`,
which is equally unmistakable and also costs no new keys. It was rejected
because there is nothing in flight to cancel on three of the five windows — the
user is declining an offer, not aborting an operation — and because "Not now" is
already the house word for that.*

*Only the button's TEXT changes. It stays a `StandardButton.Ok`, so its role,
its place in the row and its identity to everything that looks it up are
unchanged, and it remains the dialog's default — the key most people press to
get rid of a window still declines. Measured in all thirteen languages, in the
dark appearance's wider button font, on a screen tall enough that the window is
not at its cap: the row fits, nothing is clipped, nothing runs past the edge
(`tests/test_usb_driver_dialog.py::test_the_consent_buttons_fit_the_row_in_every_language`).*

### The driver window's fifth ending — an install that has not finished (A9) — ⏳ Awaiting confirmation

**Confirmed by:** *nobody yet.* Proposed 2026-09-06 by A9. Nobody has ruled on
this wording; it is recorded here because it is user-facing wording on the
driver helper, and this is where user-facing wording on that window is proposed
and ruled on.

*Deliberately NOT given an `M-` identifier, for the reason the driver consent
button's section above gives: §M is a catalogue of MESSAGES rendered from
`workflow/measurement_messages.py`, and `tests/test_message_catalogue.py`
requires every `M-` heading in this document to exist there. The driver helper
is a Preferences window, not a measurement window, and must not be given a fake
identifier to satisfy a parser.*

**What was wrong.** `core/usb_driver_installer.py::install_winusb` waited 60 s
for the elevated installer, threw away what `WaitForSingleObject` returned, then
read `GetExitCodeProcess` — which answers `STILL_ACTIVE` (259) for a process
that has not finished. `259 != 0`, so the window said the install had **failed**
and offered **Try Zadig**. Measured on the bench 2026-09-06 against a real
driverless X-Rite i1Studio on an idle 2-core ARM64 VM, a *successful* install
took **48.6 s** (`00:41:24.501` → `00:42:13.129`) — 11.4 s inside that budget,
most of it Windows making a system restore point. On a machine that is actually
busy the window would have called a succeeding install a failure and sent the
user to replace a driver that was being installed as they read it.

**The window now has a fifth ending**, alongside *It worked* / *cannot tell you
whether that changed anything* / *did not take* / *failed or was cancelled*. It
is reached when ChromIQ stops WATCHING — because its five-minute budget ran out,
or because the user pressed the button that says so. It never says "failed", it
names no instrument, and it offers no Zadig button.

> **ChromIQ stopped waiting, and cannot tell you whether that worked.**
>
> The installer had not finished when ChromIQ stopped watching it. Nothing was
> cancelled and nothing was undone. Windows is very likely still installing the
> driver, and it may well finish on its own.
>
> Give it a moment, then open **Instrument drivers** in Preferences again and
> use **Check again**. That looks your instrument up afresh and says whether the
> driver is attached now.

*No instrument is named because there is nothing to point at:
`unbound_targets()` is deliberately not asked while an install is in flight — it
samples the same device stack wdi-simple is re-enumerating and can be wrong in
either direction. No Zadig button, because nudging somebody to replace a driver
while an elevated installer is still putting one in is the one action here that
could leave the machine worse than it started. Both onward controls are named
from the controls' own `tr()` keys via `_in_prose`, the same way the reboot
window and the "cannot tell" ending are, so they cannot drift from the buttons
in any of the twelve languages.*

**And the window that is on screen while it waits.** The install used to hold
the GUI thread: `Get-Process ChromIQ` reported `Responding = False` for ~50 s
with no spinner, no message and no cursor change, and the owner read it as a
hang (*"after confirming the uac nothing seems to happen"*, then *"it seems to
be hanging"*).

| what it says | when |
|---|---|
| **Installing the driver for {name}. Windows makes a restore point before it touches a driver, and that is most of the wait.** | from the first moment there is anything to wait for |
| button: **Stop waiting** | on that window |

*The window appears only once there is a wait — an install that ends at the
permission prompt takes 2-5 s and gets nothing flashed at it. It is
application-modal, which is what stops a second install, a closed Preferences
window or a quit while an elevated installer is running.*

*The button is **Stop waiting** and not Qt's **Cancel**. The section above
rejects `Cancel` on this window's other five offers because "there is nothing in
flight to cancel … the user is declining an offer, not aborting an operation".
Here something IS in flight — and it still cannot be cancelled: an elevated
driver install cannot be safely killed, and ChromIQ does not try. The button
stops ChromIQ watching, which is what it says, and the ending above says the
same thing again in a sentence. **Not now** was considered and is wrong for the
same reason: nothing is being offered.*

**And a sixth sentence, for an instrument ChromIQ never got to.** `Reinstall
Driver` runs over every detected instrument, one permission prompt each, and the
run stops after five of the endings — the user said No, Windows would not ask, or
an elevated installer may still be running and starting a second one while it
holds Windows' PnP install lock is a way to make a good install fail. Whatever
the instruments that WERE tried have earned, this is appended:

> ChromIQ stopped before it reached {names}. Nothing was tried there, and
> nothing was changed.

*It exists because the shipped code did the skipping SILENTLY and then blamed
the skipped instrument: `all(install_winusb(d) for d in targets)` is a
generator, so the first falsy answer ended the iteration, and the untried
instrument came back from `unbound_targets()` to be named in "the driver still
isn't bound to {names}" — a sentence about an install that never happened. It is
one sentence with no count and no pronoun, so it reads for one instrument and for
four without a singular/plural pair, the same way the "isn't bound to" sentence
beside it already does.*

*The permission prompt itself is still frozen time — `SEE_MASK_NOASYNC` makes
`ShellExecuteExW` block until the shell operation completes, so ChromIQ does not
pump events while Windows asks for consent. That is deliberate: consent must
stay a modal, deliberate act. It is a second or two, not fifty.*

### The measurement guard's "{where}" — a preposition glued to a translated noun (AGENT-BD) — ⏳ Awaiting confirmation

**Confirmed by:** *nobody yet.* Recorded 2026-09-05 by AGENT-BD. **No wording is
being proposed here** — every sentence below is the wording that already
shipped, re-cut so that each language can inflect it. It is recorded because
part of it is a §M concern and because the sibling defect named at the end is
one somebody has to rule on.

ChromIQ's driver helper refuses to open during a measurement and says why. That
paragraph used to be built by formatting `core.instrument_lease.where_label()`'s
noun phrase into `"…is being read right now, from {where}."` English survives
that, and German survives it only because both labels were hand-inflected into
the dative to fit. Rendered from the shipped catalogues, four languages did not:

| | what it produced | what the language needs |
|---|---|---|
| it | da la scheda Misura | **dalla** scheda Misura |
| pt | a partir de o separador Medir | a partir **do** separador Medir |
| pl | z karcie Pomiar | z **karty** Pomiar (genitive) |
| ru | из вкладке «Измерение» | из **вкладки** «Измерение» (genitive) |

*Nothing in the project could see it. `tests/test_i18n.py` sees a key that is
present, translated, and whose placeholder matches. `scripts/i18n_extract.py`
sees nothing at all — the broken sentences exist nowhere as literals, they are
assembled at run time, so no translator was ever shown one.*

*Hand-inflecting the label was the German fix (`8d5b8430`) and it cannot
generalise: two different sentences interpolate the same label with two
different prepositions, and a language with cases needs a different form of the
noun in each. So the WHOLE SENTENCE is the translatable unit now — one complete
sentence per holder, with nothing formatted into it — and each language writes
its own preposition, article and case. It is also its own paragraph rather than
glued to the next with a space, because ja and zh join sentences with 。and no
space: even joining two translated sentences is a decision the code must not
make on a translator's behalf.*

**The sibling, which is NOT fixed and needs a ruling.** `M-INSTRUMENT-BUSY`
("ChromIQ is measuring in {where}") is fed by the same `where_label()` and has
the identical fault — "in la scheda Misura", "in o separador Medir", "in karcie
Pomiar", "in вкладке «Измерение»" — and it is worse, because that sentence is
still the English source in eleven of the twelve catalogues. It is a §M message,
so its wording is not an implementer's to change; it is raised here and left
alone.

### M-CAL-REQUESTED · PROPOSED · the placement window of a calibration the user asked for during a measurement — Measure, ChromIQ engine, strip and patch by patch

*New 2026-10-03. Knut, #182 5965478577 and 5965735823, and Basti, 5965500670, approved the behaviour: K, or the optional Calibrate button (Preferences ▸ Measurement, off by default), takes a new instrument calibration between strips or patches, on ChromIQ's own engine only, without ending the measurement. The window is NOT "Calibration required": readings exist, so its Cancel is "Cancel calibration" and keeps measuring (it sends `{"cmd":"cal_cancel"}`, never Esc, so it never marks the session as ended by the user), and it plays no sound (Knut). The instruction for the instrument itself, `calibration_instructions_html`, is shown under this text, as in "Calibration required". The wording is ours.*

> **Calibrate the Instrument**
>
> You asked for a new calibration. Everything you have measured so far is already saved.
>
> Place the instrument as described below, then press “Start Calibration”. When it is done, you carry on with the strip or patch you were on.
>
> If you change your mind, press “Cancel calibration”: nothing is measured, and you keep measuring with the calibration the instrument already has.

### M-CAL-REQUESTED-DONE · PROPOSED · the short "carry on" Calibration complete, after a calibration the user asked for — Measure

*New 2026-10-03, with M-CAL-REQUESTED. The four existing "Calibration complete" windows explain how to start measuring, which the user is already doing; this one says only that the measurement goes on, with the same key list (K included). Shown only when the instrument asked to be placed; a calibration that needed no step from the user says so in the log and the status line.*

> **Calibration Complete**
>
> The instrument has a new calibration. Carry on measuring from where you were: the reader is waiting for the same strip or patch as before.

### M-CAL-REQUESTED-FAILED · PROPOSED · a calibration the user asked for did not succeed, and reading is locked — Measure

*New 2026-10-03, with M-CAL-REQUESTED. Reading is LOCKED until a calibration succeeds: an i1Pro measures its white straight into its calibration and checks it only afterwards (`i1pro_imp.c:2230`, `2429-2433`), so after a failure it would read on without an error against a wrong reference (challenge, 2026-10-03, 1c). Try again sends another calibrate; Save and stop runs the save chain directly, as Patch Read Failed's Save Partial & Quit does (`measurement_exit_strategy.md` note 1). Closing the window leaves the lock in place, and the status line says that K, Calibrate or Stop are the ways on. `{reason}` is the instrument's own sentence, or "the calibration was cancelled" when a second attempt was cancelled at its placement prompt. The sound is Instrument error (`measurement_window_sounds.md`, awaiting confirmation).*

> **The Calibration Did Not Succeed**
>
> The instrument could not be calibrated.
>
> Everything you measured before this is saved. Nothing more is read until a calibration succeeds, because a calibration that went wrong part of the way through can leave the instrument holding values that would make every following reading wrong, without any error to show for it.
>
> •  Try again: place the instrument as asked and calibrate once more.
>
> •  Save and stop: end the measurement with what you have measured. You can carry on later with “Refine / resume existing measurement (-r)”.
>
> What the instrument reported: {reason}

### M-CHART-PATTERN-REFUSED · PROPOSED · a strip or patch pattern the readers cannot use — Create Chart, under the preview

*New 2026-10-03, forum report (strip pattern "0-9", 14 strips, "Bad location field value '(null)' on patch 266"). ChromIQ prints its labels with its own rule (letters when the pattern contains "A-Z", otherwise 1, 2, 3 ...) while ArgyllCMS chartread and ChromIQ's engine read them with ArgyllCMS's pattern grammar, so any pattern whose labels differ from the printed ones makes a chart that cannot be measured. A NEW layout (Generate Chart, the live preview, a patch set loaded or applied from the Editor) is now refused for such a pattern: the box turns red, this sentence stands under the preview, and Generate Chart is unavailable. Not a window, and nothing in the log while typing: it follows every keystroke. Restore Used Chart still redraws a chart already printed. `{reason}` is one sentence naming the pattern and what is wrong with it (too few labels for the chart's strips or patches, a label ArgyllCMS names differently from the one printed, a location whose strip and patch cannot be told apart, or a pattern ArgyllCMS cannot read at all). Shown before approval, like the other texts of this list, because it protects a chart from being printed unreadable.*

> **This strip or patch pattern cannot be used**
>
> {reason} Generate Chart stays unavailable until the pattern is changed.

### M-CHART-LOCATIONS-UNREADABLE · PROPOSED · a printed chart whose locations its patterns cannot read — Measure tab, before any reader starts

*New 2026-10-03, the same forum report seen from the Measure tab, on a sheet already printed with such a pattern. Before Start launches any reader, the chart's own SAMPLE_LOC values are checked against its STRIP_INDEX_PATTERN and PATCH_INDEX_PATTERN exactly as chartread checks them, and a chart ChromIQ laid out must also carry, at every patch, the label its patterns give that strip and patch. When it does not, no reader is started, so there is no fallback to stock chartread either (it reads the chart the same way and would fail a second time, or file the readings under the wrong patches without an error). `{detail}` names the first location that does not fit.*

> **This chart cannot be measured**
>
> This chart's patch locations do not fit its strip and patch patterns: {detail}.
>
> ArgyllCMS chartread would refuse the chart before the first patch, or file the readings under the wrong patches, and ChromIQ's own measuring engine reads it the same way. So ChromIQ has not started a measurement, and nothing has been changed.
>
> The chart was laid out with a strip or patch pattern that ArgyllCMS reads differently from the labels printed on the sheet. To measure, generate the chart again with the default patterns (A-Z, A-Z for strips and 0-9,@-9,@-9;1-999 for patches) and print it again.

### M-CHART-LEGACY-STOCK · PROPOSED · a sheet only ChromIQ's engine can read, with ArgyllCMS chartread selected — Measure tab, before any reader starts

*New 2026-10-03. Knut, #182 5965589190 Q2: a sheet printed with ChromIQ's labels from before 4.3.3-beta.7 is read by ChromIQ's own engine as printed, without changing the chart file, while a user of stock chartread is told plainly that chartread cannot read it. Nothing is started. `{detail}` names the first location that does not fit.*

> **ArgyllCMS chartread cannot read this chart**
>
> This chart's patch locations do not fit its strip and patch patterns: {detail}.
>
> The labels were printed by an earlier version of ChromIQ, and ArgyllCMS chartread reads them differently from the sheet, so it would refuse the chart or file the readings under the wrong patches. ChromIQ's own measuring engine reads the labels as they are printed.
>
> Right now, “ChromIQ chart-reading engine” in Preferences → Measurement is switched off, so ArgyllCMS chartread reads your charts. Switch it on and this chart measures normally. Nothing has been started or changed.

### M-CHART-LEGACY-ENDED · PROPOSED · the engine run on such a sheet ended, and there is no second reader — Measure, the log and the status line

*New 2026-10-03, the same ruling. When the engine stops on a sheet only it can read, none of the three fallbacks to stock chartread is made (immediate, whole-sheet mode, the mid-run resume), so the two fallback messages, one of which promises that every measured strip will be kept, are not shown. The words follow M-CR30-READ-ENDED. `{reason}` is the engine's own sentence.*

> **The measurement stopped**
>
> Reading this chart has stopped before it finished.
>
> This chart's labels were printed by an earlier version of ChromIQ in a way ArgyllCMS chartread cannot read, so there is no second reader to try, and ChromIQ has not started it.
>
> Nothing you have already measured is lost: every patch that was read is on disk, and you can carry on from it by ticking “Refine / resume existing measurement (-r)” before you press Start again.
>
> What went wrong: {reason}

### M-AUTOSAVE-NOT-SAVED · PROPOSED · the engine could not save the readings after a strip — the Measure log

*New 2026-10-21, 4.3.8 beta 3 (M3, jctay's Windows log of 2026-10-20: the engine's save after an accepted strip failed with `autosave_rename` and nothing told anyone). The engine now replaces the `.ti3` in one step and waits out a file held for a moment (about a second); when even that fails it keeps `<name>.ti3.cqtmp`, which holds every accepted strip, and reports it. The session goes on, so the text is a log line, not a window. Loading the chart or pressing Start puts a kept temporary file that is newer than the `.ti3` in its place, so a resume uses it. `{name}` is the measurement's file name, `{temp}` the kept file's name, `{code}` the system's error number.*

> **The readings could not be saved**
>
> ChromIQ could not save the readings to {name} (error {code}). Nothing is lost: every strip read so far is kept in {temp}, ChromIQ tries again after the next strip, and resuming this measurement uses that file.

### M-AUTOSAVE-RETRYING · PROPOSED · the line under the chart while the engine's automatic save has failed — the Measure tab

*New 2026-10-21, 4.3.8 beta 3 (M3). Basti, 2026-10-21: when the automatic save fails (M-AUTOSAVE-NOT-SAVED), the line under the chart, "Auto-save on, every strip is written to disk the moment it is accepted", must turn into a warning that the last save failed and will be retried, and return to normal after a later save that works. Shown in place of that line (`TiffPreview.set_notice(..., warn=True)`, on the app's warning colours: amber with near-black text in Light and Dark, Neutral's accent pairing), from the engine's `autosave_rename` error until its next `saved` event, which brings the usual line back. Shown in the beta, translated, while the wording awaits approval. The title is for the catalogue; the line shows the text.*

> **Auto-save did not work, ChromIQ tries again**
>
> ⚠  Auto-save did not work: the latest readings could not be written to the measurement file. Nothing is lost. Every strip read so far is kept in a temporary file beside it, and ChromIQ tries to save again after the next strip, so you can keep measuring. If this line stays, another program (a virus scanner or a cloud sync folder, for example) may be holding the file; the log on this tab names it.

Which lines: the headline, line 1, (for a patch the neighbour check also suspects, M-PATCH-NEIGHBOUR's lines 2 to 5 with "It also does not fit"), a blank line, lines 2 and 3 for two readings or lines 4 and 5 for more, a blank line, lines 6 and 7, a blank line, and "(Preferences ▸ Measurement, “Flag a patch…”)". Example: "Red outline: the readings do not agree / ΔE\*ab 150.4 now; before: 120.3 / / The two readings are not similar, / and both are past your limit 95.0. / / Read it again: a reading that matches / one of them shows which value is real."*

> The two readings are not similar,
> and both are past the patch error limit ({limit}).
> The {n} readings are not similar,
> and all are past the patch error limit ({limit}).

### M-REPORT-THROUGH-PROFILE · PROPOSED · a verification printed through its profile, judged against its source colours and its profile's prediction — Measurement Report (window and PDF), #182 beta 12

The ruling is CONFIRMED (`verification_printing_and_target.md` B3, `measurement_report_limits.md` §58); the words are ours and wait here. The headline heads the new table of the detailed section and the new block of the Overview. Line 1 heads the colour-accuracy table of such a sheet, in place of "Colour accuracy (ΔE00 against the chart's design)"; line 2 is the "Reference for the ΔE figures" row of "How this verification was produced" (`{profile}`: the source profile's file name, `{intent}`: the intent as that block names it, "relative colorimetric"); line 3 its "What this measured" row; line 4 stands under the Profile accuracy table; line 5 replaces the table when the profile's prediction cannot be worked out (the profile changed since the print, another light, a calibration that cannot be read again).* *Beta 15: line 4 revised for k40 (Knut 6059912998, answer 1: a failed Profile accuracy table fails the sheet; it said "these words do not change the sheet's verdict"). Lines 6 to 9 are new for k41 (answer 2), a sheet printed through the perceptual or saturation intent: line 6 replaces line 2 and line 7 replaces line 3 there, and lines 8 and 9 are the note on its five colour-accuracy rows, which are shown for information (`measurement_report_limits.md` 58.8 and 58.9).*

> **Profile accuracy (ΔE00 against the profile's own prediction)**
>
> Colour accuracy (ΔE00 against the colours the sheet was converted from)
> the colours the sheet was converted from: the chart's colours in {profile}, {intent}. Only the colours inside the profile's gamut ({intent}) are judged; the others are shown beyond the gamut, for information.
> two things: how faithfully the colours inside the profile's gamut were reproduced, and how accurate the profile is against its own prediction
> Every patch, inside the gamut or not, compared with what the profile predicts for the ink amounts that were really printed. Judged with the same limits, and a value over its limit here also fails the sheet's overall verdict.
> The profile's prediction of this sheet could not be worked out, so the profile's accuracy is not shown.
> the colours the sheet was converted from: the chart's colours in {profile}, {intent}. The sheet was printed with a rendering intent that changes colours on purpose, so this comparison is shown for information only and is not judged.
> how accurate the profile is against its own prediction. The rendering intent changed the colours on purpose, so how closely they match the original colours is shown for information only
> This sheet was printed with the perceptual rendering intent, which changes colours on purpose so that all of them fit inside the printer's gamut. So this value compares the print with the original colours for information only and is not judged against a limit. The sheet is judged on its profile accuracy instead: every patch against what the profile predicts for the ink amounts that were really printed.
> This sheet was printed with the saturation rendering intent, which changes colours on purpose to make them as vivid as the printer allows. So this value compares the print with the original colours for information only and is not judged against a limit. The sheet is judged on its profile accuracy instead: every patch against what the profile predicts for the ink amounts that were really printed.

### M-CHART-SLOW-NO-PROFILE · PROPOSED · the "taking longer than usual" window of a chart built WITHOUT a pre-conditioning profile — Create Chart, while targen runs

*New 2026-10-08, beta 12. The window that offers the faster patch layout when targen runs long (`ui/dialogs/slow_chart_dialog.py`) had one text, written for a refinement chart: it said the slowdown happens "with certain pre-conditioning profiles", promised "the same profile", and judged the quality "for a refinement chart". It also appears for a plain CMYK chart with no profile at all (beta-11 targen review, -d4 with an ink limit), where all three are wrong. A build that passes targen a profile (-c) keeps the existing text unchanged; a build without one shows this text instead, which names only what applies. The headline and the three buttons are the existing ones.*

> **This chart is taking longer than usual**
>
> ChromIQ hasn't frozen: your chart is still being built in the background. On larger (multi-page) charts, Argyll's standard way of arranging the colour patches can slow down dramatically, and that's what's happening here.
>
> You have three choices:
>
> • Keep waiting: let it finish with the highest-quality patch layout. Be aware this may take a very long time, and there's no reliable way to predict how long.
>
> • Rebuild with the faster layout (recommended): ChromIQ stops this attempt and immediately rebuilds the same chart, with the same number of patches, using a different patch-arrangement method that doesn't suffer from this slowdown. The patches are still spread evenly through the colour space, and it usually finishes in under a second.
>
> • Cancel: stop building the chart. Nothing is saved.

### M-RESUME-LAYOUT-DIFFERS · PROPOSED · Refine / resume on a measurement whose readings do not fit the chart's layout — Measure tab, Start, before anything is archived or opened

*Text review of 4.3.5 beta 9: the first sentence says the readings "do not sit where this chart prints their patch" for "are not filed under the place where this chart prints that patch" (plainer). Still proposed.*

*New 2026-10-15, issue #211. ChromIQ's engine and ArgyllCMS chartread resume BY LOCATION: for each patch of the chart they take the first row of the .ti3 with that SAMPLE_LOC, and write one row per patch of the chart with the chart's id and device values. A measurement converted from i1Profiler named its 1,680 patches A1 … T21 on each of four pages, so the resume put 420 readings on whatever this chart prints at those places, dropped 1,260, and the shrink check (§3b) put the old file back with the session's new readings in it. Measuring a sheet another program printed is out of scope (Basti, 2026-10-15), so ChromIQ refuses the resume before anything happens. `{wrong}` counts the rows that would not survive as the same patch (a location the chart does not have, one an earlier row already holds, or one where the chart prints another SAMPLE_ID), `{rows}` the file's rows, `{tab}` the Build Profile tab's name. `measurement_pairing.resume_fit`, `TabMeasure._blocked_by_a_misfitting_measurement`.*

> **This measurement does not fit this chart**
>
> ChromIQ cannot carry on with this run's measurement, because {wrong} of its {rows} readings do not sit where this chart prints their patch.
>
> This usually means the measurement was made with another program on a sheet that program printed and laid out its own way, for example a chart printed and read in i1Profiler, and was then converted or imported into this run. The readings themselves are fine, and a profile can be built from them. But carrying on puts the readings back onto this chart's patches by their place on the sheet, and on this chart those places hold other patches: readings would land on the wrong patches, and some would be dropped.
>
> What you can do:
> •  Build the profile from the measurement as it is, on the {tab} tab. Nothing about it needs to change for that.
> •  To read some patches again, read them in the program that printed the sheet, and import its new measurement into ChromIQ again.
> •  Or print this run's chart from ChromIQ and measure it from the start, with “Refine / resume existing measurement (-r)” switched off.
>
> Nothing has been measured, and nothing has been changed.

*With `{wrong}` = 1:*

> ChromIQ cannot carry on with this run's measurement, because 1 of its {rows} readings does not sit where this chart prints its patch.
>
> This usually means the measurement was made with another program on a sheet that program printed and laid out its own way, for example a chart printed and read in i1Profiler, and was then converted or imported into this run. The readings themselves are fine, and a profile can be built from them. But carrying on puts the readings back onto this chart's patches by their place on the sheet, and on this chart that place holds another patch: a reading would land on the wrong patch, or be dropped.
>
> What you can do:
> •  Build the profile from the measurement as it is, on the {tab} tab. Nothing about it needs to change for that.
> •  To read some patches again, read them in the program that printed the sheet, and import its new measurement into ChromIQ again.
> •  Or print this run's chart from ChromIQ and measure it from the start, with “Refine / resume existing measurement (-r)” switched off.
>
> Nothing has been measured, and nothing has been changed.

### M-REPORT-PAPER-WHITE-DOUBT · PROPOSED · a warning under the paper white of a measurement whose paper patch reads much darker than its lightest patch · Measurement Report (window and PDF), 4.3.5 beta 8

*Text review of 4.3.5 beta 9: "{dl} L* lighter" (the unit was missing), and the last sentence in plainer order. Still proposed.*

*New 2026-10-15 (#210, Basti: "when the paper-white patch is far from white, WARN clearly (which patch, its values, why it looks wrong) and keep going; coloured papers must still work"). Shown in "Detailed data per measurement", under "Paper white and darkest black", when another reading of the same measurement is more than 8 L* lighter than the paper patch (`measurement_report.PAPER_WHITE_DOUBT_DL`). Lightness against the sheet's own lightest reading, not against white, so cream and coloured papers never trip it: ink only darkens the paper. The report is worked out with that paper white all the same. Report text (K18): causes, no ChromIQ how-to. {loc}, {L}, {a}, {b}: the paper patch; {lighter_loc}, {lighter_L}: the lightest reading; {dl}: the difference. Wording ours; shown from 4.3.5 beta 8.*

> **This paper white does not look like paper**
>
> The paper white of this measurement comes from patch {loc}, the patch printed with no ink. It was measured at L* {L}, a* {a}, b* {b}, while patch {lighter_loc} of the same measurement reads L* {lighter_L}, which is {dl} L* lighter.
>
> Ink can only make paper darker, so the patch with no ink is normally the lightest patch of the sheet, or within a few L* of it. That holds for white, cream and coloured papers alike, because the paper's own colour is in every patch. A difference this large usually means the reading of {loc} is not a reading of the bare paper: the instrument may have slipped by a patch along the strip, a strip may have been read in the wrong place, or the chart may have been printed with colour management, which puts ink on the paper patch too.
>
> The results of this measurement are worked out with this paper white all the same, so every value that is judged relative to the paper may be off: read this measurement's figures above with that in mind.

### M-PRINT-WIN-INKS-NOT-POSTSCRIPT · PROPOSED · a window when ChromIQ's own Windows route would send a CMYK or multi-ink chart to a printer that does not understand PostScript · Print Chart tab, Windows, 4.3.8

*New 2026-10-20. Windows only, ChromIQ's own route or the Windows print dialog route (#205, Basti 2026-10-10: Windows gets the macOS switch, "Use default Windows printer dialog", the dialog staying the default). Wording ours; shown from 4.3.8 beta 2 on, translated into all thirteen languages (Knut 6166519230). Measured and driven on Windows 11 25H2 ARM64 (report folder `~/Desktop/ChromIQ-work/2026-10-20_205_windows_direct_print`). With the switch off, a printer whose driver is not PostScript (its data file is no PPD, `win_spooler.DriverFacts.is_postscript`) can only be printed to through its driver, which takes RGB (GDI). An RGB chart is then handed to the Windows print dialog opened on that printer; a chart that is not RGB (`chart_inks.is_rgb_page`, from the ink list) gets this window and nothing is sent, no print record (`_commit_print_record(False)`). The same rule as `ChartIsNotRGB` on the macOS dialog route. {printer}: the queue; {inks}: `chart_inks.ink_set_label` ("CMYK, 4 inks", "CMYK + Orange + Green, 6 inks"). The TIFF files in the run folder hold the chart's own values with no profile (issue #205), which is what a RIP prints.*

> **This printer cannot print this chart unchanged**
>
> {printer} does not understand PostScript, so ChromIQ can only send it the chart through its printer driver, and that driver accepts RGB colours only. This chart has {inks}. On the way through the driver every patch would be converted into RGB, so the printed sheet would no longer match the chart file, and a measurement of it would describe colours that were never printed.
>
> Nothing was printed.
>
> What you can do:
> • Print this chart on a PostScript printer.
> • Print it from a RIP (printing software that controls the printer itself): the chart is stored as TIFF files in the run folder, with its own colour values.
> • Or make an RGB chart for this printer in step 1.

### M-STRIP-PART-SLIPPED-LATE · PROPOSED · the Strip may be misaligned window, when part of a strip was read one patch late — Measure tab, strip mode, ChromIQ engine, "Warn me if a strip looks misaligned" on

*New 2026-10-22 (4.3.10), forum post 149786. jctay's i1Pro 3 read strip 36 of a 585-patch verification chart with 36A to 36H one patch late (36A read the paper) and the rest of the strip in step, and nothing warned him: the engine's net (`cq_detect_misalign`) only tries whole-strip shifts. `workflow/slipped_strip.py` tries runs of four or more neighbouring patches with the net's own thresholds (`MeasureManager._check_part_of_strip_slipped`); on a chart in plain order ("Preserve Patch Order") a run along a ramp has to be far wrong (25 ΔE76 as read, and fit at least 3.3 times better shifted). {strip} is the strip label, {base} the run's mean ΔE00 against its own expected colours, {best} against the neighbouring patches'. {remeasure}, {keep}, {stop} are the window's three buttons, the same as the whole-strip "Strip may be misaligned" window's.*

*Revised 2026-10-22 (4.3.10, agent 14's review, approved by Basti 2026-10-22): the figures are **ΔE00**, the unit of the Measurement Report's tables (the search itself still judges in CIE76, as the engine's net does), averaged over exactly the patches {first} to {last}; the one patch the slip pushed out of step is named apart in {lead_line} (`slip_lead_line`: "Patch {lead} came out with the colour of the white paper. " when it read the paper, else "Patch {lead} came out wrong as well, with a colour that is neither its own nor its neighbour's. ", or nothing). *New 2026-10-22 (4.3.10, agent 14's review, approved by Basti 2026-10-22). The engine files a strip in the direction its colours fit best (`"reversed": true`), and one that slipped by a patch can fit the wrong direction better: on screen all 13 patches of a slipped strip 36 were stored reversed and nothing asked; in #210's data (Chart-192-Patches-new) strip 13 is such a strip. The check also tries the readings taken in the opposite order, in step or one patch out (two touching stretches allowed, most of the strip required).*

*Revised 2026-10-22 (4.3.10, agent 14's review, approved by Basti 2026-10-22): the figures are **ΔE00**, the unit of the Measurement Report's tables (the search itself still judges in CIE76, as the engine's net does), averaged over exactly the patches {first} to {last}; the one patch the slip pushed out of step is named apart in {lead_line} (`slip_lead_line`: "Patch {lead} came out with the colour of the white paper. It now says that patches {first} to {last} hold the readings of other patches and that only a patch in the middle can still hold its own; and "the expected colours of the patches at those places" is spelled out as first against last, second against the one before the last.*

*Revised 2026-10-23 (4.3.11, review 36, the coordinator's ruling): since 4.3.11 the engine's own net also asks this question, and it finds strips that were filed back to front AND slipped by TWO patches (on screen: a strip read two patches late came back reversed). The old sentence "(Where the reading also slipped by one patch, each reading is compared with the patch beside that place.)" was then wrong, and so was "Only a patch in the middle of the strip can still hold its own reading.", which holds only for a strip that did not slip. Now {shift_line} (`slip_shift_line`) says how far it slipped: nothing for a strip in step, "The readings also slipped by one patch on the way, so each of these comparisons moves one patch further along the strip. ", or the same with two patches. {middle_line} (`slip_middle_line`) is " Only a patch in the middle of the strip can still hold its own reading." for a strip that did not slip, else nothing. And {lead_line} names BOTH patches that hold what lies beyond a strip two patches out: "Patches {lead} and {lead2} came out with the colour of the white paper. ", or "Patches {lead} and {lead2} came out wrong as well, with colours that are neither their own nor their neighbours'. " (the same for M-STRIP-WHOLE-SLIPPED-TWO-LATE / -EARLY). Their large ΔE00 values come from that, not from the printer or the profile, and they pull the figures of this measurement up. Read strip {strip} again and make the report again.

### M-REPORT-STRIP-REVERSED · PROPOSED · the same, when a strip looks filed back to front

*New 2026-10-22 (4.3.10), see M-STRIP-REVERSED.*

*Revised 2026-10-22 (4.3.10, agent 14's review, approved by Basti 2026-10-22): the figures are **ΔE00**, the unit of the Measurement Report's tables (the search itself still judges in CIE76, as the engine's net does), averaged over exactly the patches {first} to {last}; the one patch the slip pushed out of step is named apart in {lead_line} (`slip_lead_line`: "Patch {lead} came out with the colour of the white paper. " when it read the paper, else "Patch {lead} came out wrong as well, with a colour that is neither its own nor its neighbour's. ", or nothing). Shown from the beta that proposes it, translated into all thirteen languages.*

*Revised 2026-10-22 (4.3.10, agent 17, the reviewer's finding): the old wording said that none of the strip's patches held its own reading, which is untrue for a strip with a middle patch (taken the other way round, that patch is compared with itself, so it can keep its own reading). It now says that patches {first} to {last} hold the readings of other patches and that only a patch in the middle can still hold its own; and "the expected colours of the patches at those places" is spelled out as first against last, second against the one before the last.*

> **Strip {strip} looks filed back to front**
>
> The readings of strip {strip} match its patches far better when they are taken the other way round, from its last patch back to its first. {lead_line}For patches {first} to {last} that is {best} ΔE00 against {base} ΔE00 on average. Taken the other way round means that the reading of the strip's first patch is compared with the expected colour of its last patch, the reading of its second patch with the patch before the last, and so on (where the reading also slipped by one patch, with the patch beside that place). The strip was probably filed in the wrong direction (this can happen when a reading slips by one patch), so patches {first} to {last} hold the readings of other patches of the strip, not their own. Only a patch in the middle of the strip can still hold its own reading. The large ΔE00 values of these patches come from that, not from the printer or the profile, and they pull the figures of this measurement up. Read strip {strip} again and make the report again.

### M-CR-VERIFICATION · PROPOSED · Check & Refine's result window, Run type Verification (the measurement is a dated verification) — Check & Refine tab

*New 2026-10-22 (4.3.10), Knut's report, Basti's ruling of 2026-10-22 (§6c-1). Shown at the top of the result window's body, titled "Profile Check Against a Verification Print", when the checked measurement is a dated verification of the open project; the second paragraph only when strips are above the limit. {guide} is the button "Guide Me Through Re-reading These Strips". The window then offers Confirm and that button only: no pre-conditioning, no install, no scanner-target files. The first paragraph and its headline are also written at the top of the saved Quality_Check report. Shown from the beta that proposes it, translated into all thirteen languages.*

> **Checked against a verification print**
>
> This check compares the profile with a verification measurement: a chart that was printed and measured after the profile was built, so the profile has never seen these readings. For every patch, the check takes the RGB values that were sent to the printer, works out through the profile the colour they should give, and compares it with the colour that was measured. So the figures show how well the profile describes your printer and paper on the day of this print, not how closely it fits the data it was built from. They are usually somewhat higher than a check of the profiling measurement.
>
> {guide}: takes you to the Measure tab with this verification selected and guides you through re-reading the strips listed here. The new readings replace the old ones of those strips in this verification measurement, so you can run the check again afterwards. The profile itself is not changed, and nothing is added to the profiling run.

### M-STRIP-FAILED-TOO-MANY · PROPOSED · Strip Read Failed, the driver reported “Too many patches” — Measure tab, strip mode

*New 2026-10-21, 4.3.8 (B1 and M1, forum 149774; agent 1's analysis of jctay's log). **Basti approved the behaviour on 2026-10-21** (approver while Knut is away): the Strip Read Failed window gives each error its own cause and remedy instead of the one text for all ("scan more slowly and steadily, or raise the Patch consistency tolerance", which does not help "Too many patches"), and says that the instrument's button can be used when the connected instrument supports it. The causes are taken from where the drivers raise each error (i1pro_imp.c:6974-7026, 7160-7201, 6596; the same in munki_imp.c and i1pro3_imp.c). The window shows the headline in bold and the body under it, then M-STRIP-FAILED-BUTTON when the engine's misread event carries `"button_retry": true` (i1Pro, i1Pro 2, i1Pro 3 and 3 Plus, ColorMunki), then the approved button lines (Retry, Skip Strip, Save Partial & Quit), unchanged. `{reason}` is the driver's own sentence. Which text: `core.measure_pace.misread_kind`. The wording is ours and waits here; it is shown from the beta that proposes it. A patch-size change to the chart layout was deferred by Basti and is not part of this.*

> **The instrument found more patches than this strip has**
>
> While you move along the strip, the instrument looks for the places where the colour changes, and counts a patch between each two of them. This time it counted more patches than are printed on the strip. It could then not tell which reading belongs to which patch, so it kept none of them. The strips you have already read are not affected.
>
> This usually has one of these causes:
> • The movement was not even. A pause, a hesitation or a change of speed in the middle of the strip looks like one more colour change.
> • Two neighbouring patches have very similar colours. The narrow divider printed between them can then be counted as a patch of its own. If the same strip fails again and again while the others read well, this is the most likely reason.
> • The patches are small. The closer they are to the smallest size your instrument can read, the more easily this happens.
>
> What to do: put the instrument down on the white paper before the first patch. If your instrument gives a short beep when it is ready, wait for it. Then move in one smooth movement at an even speed, and keep going until the instrument is on the white paper after the last patch. Try not to stop or slow down on the way. A ruler or a straight edge along the strip helps to keep the movement straight and even.
>
> What the instrument reported: {reason}

### M-STRIP-FAILED-TOO-FEW · PROPOSED · Strip Read Failed, the driver reported “Not enough patches” — Measure tab, strip mode

*New 2026-10-21, B1/M1, see M-STRIP-FAILED-TOO-MANY.*

> **The instrument found fewer patches than this strip has**
>
> While you move along the strip, the instrument looks for the places where the colour changes, and counts a patch between each two of them. This time it found fewer patches than are printed on the strip. It could then not match its readings to the patches, so it kept none of them. The strips you have already read are not affected.
>
> This usually has one of these causes:
> • The movement started after the first patch or stopped before the last one, so a patch at one end was never seen.
> • The movement was too quick, so a patch passed under the instrument before it could take enough readings of it.
> • Two neighbouring patches have very similar colours, so the instrument did not notice the change from one to the other.
>
> What to do: put the instrument down on the white paper before the first patch. If your instrument gives a short beep when it is ready, wait for it. Then move steadily, a little more slowly than last time if you were quick, and keep going until the instrument is on the white paper after the last patch.
>
> What the instrument reported: {reason}

### M-STRIP-FAILED-INCONSISTENT · PROPOSED · Strip Read Failed, the driver reported “Reading is inconsistent” — Measure tab, strip mode

*New 2026-10-21, B1/M1, see M-STRIP-FAILED-TOO-MANY.*

> **The readings of one patch did not agree with each other**
>
> Your instrument takes many readings of each patch as it moves along the strip. On this strip, the readings of at least one patch differed from each other by more than the patch consistency tolerance allows, so the instrument rejected the strip and kept none of it. The strips you have already read are not affected.
>
> This usually has one of these causes:
> • The speed changed while the instrument was on a patch, or the instrument tilted or lifted a little.
> • The instrument slid to one side, so part of a patch was read from the strip next to it. Narrow strips make this easier to do.
> • The patch itself is not printed evenly, for example because of banding, a clogging nozzle or a mark on the paper.
>
> What to do: put the instrument flat on the white paper before the first patch. If your instrument gives a short beep when it is ready, wait for it. Then move at one even speed and keep the instrument in the middle of the strip all the way to the white paper after the last patch. A ruler or a straight edge helps.
>
> If the strip keeps failing, look at it closely. A patch that is visibly uneven means the print is the problem, and printing the chart again helps more than reading it again. On a textured paper, a higher “Patch consistency tolerance (-T)” on the Measure tab makes this check more forgiving from the next measurement on. ChromIQ starts it at 0.7, which is a little stricter than the instrument's own 1.0.
>
> What the instrument reported: {reason}

### M-STRIP-FAILED-EDGES · PROPOSED · Strip Read Failed, the driver reported “Swipe didn't start and end on the media” — Measure tab, strip mode

*New 2026-10-21, B1/M1, see M-STRIP-FAILED-TOO-MANY.*

> **The movement did not start and end on the white paper**
>
> The instrument compares what it saw at the very start of the movement with what it saw at the very end. Both should be the plain white paper before and after the strip. This time the two were too different, so the instrument could not be sure where the strip began and ended, and it kept none of the readings. The strips you have already read are not affected.
>
> This usually happens when the movement started on the first patch instead of the paper in front of it, or stopped on the last patch, or ran off the edge of the sheet at the end.
>
> What to do: put the instrument down on the white paper a little before the first patch. If your instrument gives a short beep when it is ready, wait for it. Then move along the strip and stop only when the instrument is on the white paper after the last patch.
>
> What the instrument reported: {reason}

### M-STRIP-FAILED-TOO-FAST · PROPOSED · Strip Read Failed, the driver reported “Not enough samples per patch - Slow Down!” — Measure tab, strip mode

*New 2026-10-21, B1/M1, see M-STRIP-FAILED-TOO-MANY.*

### M-STRIP-FAILED-TOO-SHORT · PROPOSED · Strip Read Failed, the driver reported “Reading is too short” — Measure tab, strip mode

*New 2026-10-21 (4.3.8 beta 4), Basti's approval of the same day: on his ColorMunki a press of the button with no swipe gives exactly "Reading is too short" (hand test `hand_test_button/result/`, 03-strip-read-failed.png), and the window gave only the general text (M-STRIP-FAILED-OTHER). The ColorMunki and i1Pro drivers raise it when the scan ended before the instrument had delivered even the minimum number of readings it asks for first (`munki_imp.c:9045`, `i1pro_imp.c:11800`, `treadings < inummeas`; about 0.1 s of readings in the ColorMunki's strip mode, `munki_imp.c:719`); in strip mode those instruments read for as long as their button is held down. Picked by `core.measure_pace.misread_kind` ("too_short"); M-STRIP-FAILED-BUTTON is added under it exactly as for the other texts. Wording ours, shown from 4.3.8 beta 4.*

> **The reading stopped almost as soon as it started**
>
> The instrument stopped reading after only a moment, before it had taken even the smallest number of readings it needs for a strip. So it could not look for any patches, and it kept nothing of this strip. The strips you have already read are not affected.
>
> This usually has one of these causes:
> • The button was pressed and let go straight away, without a movement along the strip. When you read a strip with the button, the instrument reads only for as long as you hold the button down.
> • The button was let go too early, while the instrument was still at the start of the strip.
>
> What to do: put the instrument down on the white paper before the first patch. Press the button and keep holding it down. If your instrument gives a short beep when it is ready, wait for it. Then move along the whole strip in one smooth movement at an even speed, and let go of the button only when the instrument is on the white paper after the last patch.
>
> What the instrument reported: {reason}

### Help card “Check a finished profile”: the Check & Refine step, starting a strip on the paper, and the report after re-reading · PROPOSED · Help ▸ the help cards, 4.3.10

*New 2026-10-23 (4.3.10). Approved in substance by Basti, 2026-10-23 (Knut's suggestion): the card gains a Check & Refine step (verification-aware since 4.3.10-beta.1, §6c), a note on starting every strip on the white paper rather than on its number (jctay, forum posts 149795/149800: patch A read the paper and the next patches came out one place late; agent 18's analysis), and a note to make the Measurement Report after re-reading. The subtitle loses its em dash and the Measure step names the box as it is labelled. Every button, label and claim was checked against the code: the check runs profcheck on the chart's device values, so it is right for a sheet printed raw or a FROM PROFILE GAMUT chart and warns before a sheet printed “Through the profile” (M-CM-PROFCHECK-CONVERTED, §2b of verification_printing_and_target.md); the live misalignment question needs a run of four or more patches one place out (`slipped_strip.MIN_RUN`), so the note says that a slip spoiling only the first two, three or four patches is not asked about. Same precedent as the help texts above: shown from the beta that proposes them, translated into all thirteen languages, approved afterwards (Knut 6166519230). `ui/dialogs/welcome_dialog.py`, card key `verify`.*

*Revised 2026-10-23 (4.3.10, agent 21, with the short-slip rules approved by Basti 2026-10-23): the check now also asks about a short slip next to a patch at an end of the strip that read the paper, or inside the strip where one patch was read twice, so "A slip that spoils only the first two, three or four patches of a strip is not asked about" became untrue. The note now names both kinds and says that a short slip is not always recognised (agent 19 measured from about 20 % of them found on synthetic profiling strips judged against design colours to about 95 % on verifications judged against the profile's prediction), so a strip whose first patches are outlined in red and that asked nothing is still read again.*

> **Subtitle:** Measure a check chart and see, in real numbers, how accurate your finished profile is, and whether it stays that way over time.
>
> **Step 3 (Measure):** On the Measure tab, pick “New verification” in the “Verification:” box of the Profile-run bar at the top of the window, then measure the chart as normal.
>
> **Start every strip on the white paper, not on its number**
>
> Put the instrument down on the bare white paper in front of the strip's first patch, beside the strip's number rather than on it. If your instrument gives a short beep when it is ready, wait for it. Then move in one smooth movement at an even speed, and keep going until it is on the white paper after the last patch. If it starts on the number, it can count one patch too many: the first patch then comes out with the colour of the paper, and the next ones with the colour of the patch before them.
>
> ChromIQ helps you catch this while you measure. In the preview it outlines a patch in red when its reading is far from the colour it should have (on a verification, the colour the profile predicts). And with “Warn me if a strip looks misaligned” ticked in Preferences ▸ Measurement (it is, unless you switched it off), it asks you to read a strip again when its patches look one place out: a longer run of them anywhere in the strip, and also a short slip of only a few patches, when the first or the last patch of the strip read the white paper or when one patch inside the strip was read twice. Choose “Re-measure this strip” and read the strip again before you go on: it takes a few seconds now and spares you a wrong report later. A short slip is not always recognised, because two or three patches can look like their neighbours by chance. So when the first patches of a strip are outlined in red and nothing asked, simply read that strip again.
>
> **Step (Check & Refine, optional):** Optional: on the Check & Refine tab, make sure “.ti3 test data file:” shows this verification and “ICC / ICM profile:” the run's profile, then click “Analyse Profile Quality”.
>
> **What this check tells you**
>
> You do not have to pick any files. With Run type “Verification” and a date chosen in the Profile-run bar, the two fields fill in by themselves: that date's measurement and the run's profile. (With “New verification” there is nothing to check yet, so they stay empty.)
>
> For every patch, the check takes the chart's RGB numbers, works out through the profile the colour they should give, and compares that with the colour you measured. The profile has never seen these readings, so the figures show how well it describes your printer and paper on the day of this print, not how closely it fits the data it was built from. That is why they are usually somewhat higher than a check of the profiling measurement.
>
> The figures come from ArgyllCMS's profcheck, judged with this tab's own settings (“Flag strips for re-measurement above ΔE:”, and in MANUAL also “Delta E formula:”). The Measurement Report works its figures out separately, against its own reference and its limit set, so the two do not show exactly the same numbers.
>
> **Which verification sheets this check can judge**
>
> The check sends the RGB numbers stored in the chart through the profile, so it is only right when those are the numbers the printer was sent: a verification chart printed with “Colour” set to “Raw — no profile”, or a chart made with “FROM PROFILE GAMUT”, which already has the profile applied and is printed raw. A sheet printed “Through the profile” was converted while it was printed, so its chart still holds the numbers from before the conversion. ChromIQ then warns you before the check runs, and the Measurement Report in the next step is the right way to judge that sheet.
>
> **Re-reading the patches with the largest errors**
>
> When patches are above the limit, the window “Profile Check Against a Verification Print” lists the strips they are in. A large error on one patch is either a misread or a real difference between the profile and the print, and reading it again tells the two apart.
>
> Click “← Guide Me Through Re-reading These Strips”. ChromIQ takes you to the Measure tab with this verification selected and guides you through just those strips, into the same date. When they are done, the “Re-measurement Complete” window opens: “Finish” saves the new readings in this date's own folder and ends the session, and “Continue Measuring Manually” lets you read more yourself first. A copy of the readings the date had before was put in its “old” folder when you started, so nothing is lost.
>
> Then click “Analyse Profile Quality” again. A patch that comes back with the same error was read correctly the first time: the difference is real. The profile itself is never changed, and nothing is added to the profiling run.
>
> **When there is no guide button**
>
> If no patch is above the limit, there is nothing to read again, and “Confirm” closes the window. If the verification does not belong to the project that is open (you browsed to it), the window explains how to re-read the strips by hand instead. Installing the profile and using it for pre-conditioning are not offered here: a verification only checks a profile, so those belong to the profiling run.
>
> **Make the report after you have read strips again**
>
> A report is made from the measurement as it is at the moment you generate it. So read any strips you want to read again first, and make the report after that.
>
> In its “Worst patches” table, look out for several patches of one strip near the top, each showing in “Measured” the colour that the patch before it (or after it) shows in “Expected”. That strip was read one place out. When ChromIQ finds this for a run of patches, the report says so in a paragraph right above the table, headed “Strip … looks shifted by one patch” (or “Strip … looks filed back to front”). Read that strip again on the Measure tab, then make the report again.

### M-PAGE-PAUSE · PROPOSED · the pause after the last strip of a page — Measure tab, strip mode

*New 2026-10-23, 4.3.10 (jctay, forum 149802; Basti 2026-10-23: "can this be added as an option in preferences measure tab? tooltip icon", and the same day: the pause is a review moment, also after the last strip of the chart). Preferences ▸ Measurement ▸ "Pause after each page so I can check it", off by default. With ChromIQ's reading engine, reading strips, outside guided re-measurement: after a strip is read and accepted, and any question about it answered, the engine holds (`{"event":"held"}`) instead of arming the next strip whenever the next strip to read is on another page, or the strip was the last of the chart or completed it (`MeasureManager.page_pause_plan`). The Measure tab then shows a note (Preferences ▸ Measurement ▸ "Show a note when it pauses", on by default, Basti 2026-10-23), not a window: it fades in over the lower part of the chart preview in the legend chip's see-through look and fast fade (`ui.fade.Fade`, shared with the chip; Basti 2026-10-23), so the page shows through it, and fades out once there has been time to read it (4 words a second, 8 to 30 s; Basti 2026-10-23), at the first click elsewhere or key, or at the instrument's button. With that option off the pause shows nothing extra (Basti, 2026-10-23), apart from the line in the measurement log; Return, the space bar and the instrument's button continue either way. A strip re-read from the pause brings the pause back. See `measurement_exit_strategy.md` note 11 and `measurement_window_sounds.md` §4e. The wording is ours and waits here; it is shown from the beta that proposes it. {continue} is the Continue button's own label ("Continue with page {next_page}"), {reread} the Re-read button's.*

> **Page {page} of {pages} is done: next comes page {next_page}**
>
> Before you go on, look over page {page} in the preview: a patch with a red outline has a reading that looks wrong. To read a strip again, click it in the preview or click “{reread}”. Then put page {next_page} under the instrument and click “{continue}”. The next strip to read is strip {target}.

### M-PAGE-PAUSE-END · PROPOSED · the pause after the last strip of the chart — Measure tab, strip mode

*New 2026-10-23, see M-PAGE-PAUSE. Continue lets the engine go on exactly as without the pause: once every patch has a reading, "All Strips Read" opens and the choice how to finish is made there, so the pause asks no second question.*

> **That was the last strip of the chart**
>
> Before the measurement is finished, look over the chart in the preview: a patch with a red outline has a reading that looks wrong. To read a strip again, click it in the preview or click “{reread}”. When everything looks right, click “{continue}”, and ChromIQ finishes the measurement as it always does.

*New 2026-10-23, see M-PAGE-PAUSE.*

### M-PAGE-PAUSE-BUTTON · PROPOSED · the paragraph that says the instrument's button can continue — Measure tab

*New 2026-10-23, see M-PAGE-PAUSE. Only when the engine's held event says the instrument's button can answer (i1Pro, i1Pro 2, i1Pro 3 and 3 Plus, ColorMunki). The engine reports a press only while it holds, outside any scan, so it can never start a strip; a press within 0.3 s of the pause appearing is ignored.*

>

### M-PAGE-PAUSE-HELP · PROPOSED · the ⓘ beside the pause's headline: the whole explanation — Measure tab

*New 2026-10-23, see M-PAGE-PAUSE. The note stays short, because it lies over the chart preview for a few seconds and the page under it is what is being checked; the whole explanation is here, behind the ⓘ.*

> **Why ChromIQ stops here**
>
> You switched on “Pause after each page so I can check it” in Preferences ▸ Measurement, so ChromIQ stops after the last strip of each page and after the last strip of the chart. While it waits, nothing is read: the instrument is not ready for the next strip.
>
> Look over the page: the preview still shows it. A patch with a red outline has a reading that looks wrong. With “Each patch shows: Expected & measured (split)” you can compare every patch with the colour it should have. The list in this note names the strips of the page that are worth a second look.
>
> To read a strip again, click it in the preview, or click the Re-read button, which offers the first strip worth a look. Read it as always. Once it has been read, ChromIQ stops here again, so you can check it.
>
> When the page looks right, put the next page under the instrument and click Continue. With an i1Pro, i1Pro 2, i1Pro 3 or ColorMunki you can instead press the button on the instrument once. That press only continues: it never starts reading a strip, so the next strip is read with the next press, as always. Return and the space bar continue too.
>
> This note fades away once there has been time to read it (between 8 and 30 seconds, depending on how much it says), or as soon as you click somewhere or press a key. The measurement goes on waiting until you continue.
>
> Stop works as it always does: it asks whether to keep what you have measured. To measure without these pauses, or without this note, change the two options in Preferences ▸ Measurement.

### M-PRINT-CHART-CUT · PROPOSED · a chart a little larger than its paper, where more than empty margin would be cut — Print Chart, every route

*New 2026-10-23, 4.3.10 (jctay, forum 149803: a 102 × 152 mm chart refused on the 100 × 148 mm paper of a 4 × 6 in printer; Knut 149804; Basti 2026-10-23: "ideally ... this gets printed without a warning on a printer like jctay has", and a window only "when the overhang would cut something that matters"). A chart larger than its paper by at most 5 mm and 3 % on each side is printed at exactly 100 %, with no question and a line in the log (`_OVER_PAPER_LOG`) and the print record (`outside_paper_mm`), when everything printed stays on the paper with 1 mm to spare and the blank paper the layout gave around the patches is kept up to what ArgyllCMS's printtarg leaves for the instrument (along the strips, at both ends: 10 mm i1Pro, 20 mm i1Pro 3 Plus, 25 mm ColorMunki, 25 mm DTP41, 6.35 mm DTP51; across them only the i1Pro holder's 26 mm clip border when the layout has one; ChromIQ's own 5 mm for the SpectroScan and the CR30; agent 22 against the 3.5.0 source, 2026-10-23), moved off centre when that puts the cut into an empty margin (`workflow.overhang`). Never shrunk. Otherwise this window: the Windows and macOS print dialogs print nothing ({outcome} = "Nothing was printed."); ChromIQ's own route shows it in its confirmation window, whose Print still prints at 100 % ({outcome} = the "If you print anyway" sentence). Larger than 5 mm or 3 % keeps M-PRINT-WIN-DIALOG-TOO-BIG and the size mismatch warning. {why} is one of the three sentences in M-PRINT-CHART-CUT-PARTS. See `verification_printing_and_target.md` §O (awaiting confirmation).*

> **Part of the chart would not be on this paper**
>
> The chart measures {chart}, and the paper is {paper}. ChromIQ never makes a chart smaller to fit, because every patch has to be exactly where your measuring instrument expects it. A chart only a little larger than the paper is printed at exactly 100 % when the part that does not fit is empty margin, or only things no instrument reads: the end of the thin line of small print that ArgyllCMS writes along the edge of its charts (“ArgyllCMS - Chart …”), or the short ruler marks along the edge that only help you line up a ruler.
>
> Here it is not: {why} {outcome}
>
> What you can do:
> • Print on paper of the size the chart was made for, if your printer can print it.
> • Or lay the chart out again for this paper: in Create Chart, choose this paper size (or Custom, with its width and height) and generate the chart again. The patches are then placed for this paper, and the number of patches on a page, or their size, may change. A chart laid out again is a new chart, so print and measure the new one.

### M-REPORT-EVENNESS-SPREAD · PROPOSED · why the two evenness rows read N-A because the patches do not reach far enough across the page, and the notes on a page left out for it · Measurement Report (window and PDF), the presets window and the Measure tab's pre-flight

*New 2026-10-23 (4.3.10), forum post 149811 (jctay's 4 × 6 in i1Pro card) and Basti's ruling of the same day, which replaces Knut's confirmed 60 % area floor (`measurement_report_limits.md` §16.6): a page counts for evenness when its patches reach across at least 65 % of the page's width AND at least 65 % of its height (`measurement_report.EVENNESS_MIN_PAGE_SPAN`). One line each: the report's reason when one page of 9 by 9 is left out for it, the same when several are ({w} and {h} are then the page where the patches reach furthest), the note under a row that is judged on the other pages (one page, several pages), and the presets window's line. {w}, {h} are rounded down to one decimal, {k} and {c} are the floor. Replaces "the patches on page {p} of the measured chart cover {x} % of the page; at least {k} % is needed", its plural, "The patches on page {p} cover {x} % of the page, less than {k} %, so it is not counted.", its plural and "On no page of this chart with at least {k} strips and {k} rows do the patches cover at least {c} % of the page.", which stay only for a report saved under the old rule. Shown from the beta that proposes it, translated into all thirteen languages.*

> the patches on pages {p} of the measured chart do not reach far enough across their page: on the page where they reach furthest, they reach across {w} % of its width and {h} % of its height; to compare the nine areas of a page, the patches need to reach across at least {k} % of the width and at least {k} % of the height, so that the nine areas lie spread over the whole page
> The patches on page {p} reach across {w} % of the page's width and {h} % of its height. At least {k} % is needed in both directions, so this page is not counted.
> The patches on pages {p} do not reach across at least {k} % of their page's width and at least {k} % of its height, so they are not counted.
> On no page of this chart with at least {k} strips and {k} rows do the patches reach across at least {c} % of the page's width and at least {c} % of its height, so the nine areas of a page would not lie spread over the whole page.
