### 11b-1. Confirmed behaviour — "I read strip B" counts the reading as strip B (4.3.5)

**Confirmed by:** Knut, 2026-10-10, #182 [6102031563](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6102031563) (answer 1, to question 1 of [6099862394](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6099862394): *"When I specify that I read strip B, then the values I read should be counted as strip B values and judged in the neighbour check for the strip B values ... I should not need to read it again, and then focus can stay at unread strip I was supposed to read (in this case strip C, but the reading focus arrows could have been on any other strip, f.ex. F ...). If I would have clicked "Keep it, its strip C", then the values should be counted as strip C values and judged in the neighbour check for the strip C values, and then jump to the next unread strip D."*).

* **I read strip {like}:** the reading is counted as strip {like} and judged as strip {like}: the patch error limit, the strip test, the neighbour check, the outlines, the cards, the counts and the saved measurement. It replaces {like}'s earlier reading. The reader's arrow stays on {strip}, the strip that was due (whichever strip that was), which is unread and still has to be measured.
* **Keep, it is strip {strip}:** the reading is counted and judged as strip {strip}, and the reader goes on to the next unread strip.
* **The window's line for "I read strip {like}"** describes this (M-STRIP-READ-TWICE, adjusted to this ruling).
* **Tested every time:** every way the window ends, on every chart type it can appear on (Knut, 6094941512: *"The test of the neighbour check must be constructed to verify all these choices every time this function is verified"*).

### ⏳ Awaiting confirmation — how 4.3.5 carries out "I read strip B"

**Confirmed by:** *nobody yet.*

* **In the measuring engine.** chromiq-chartread files every reading under the strip it is positioned on, so the reading is the engine's strip {strip}. The answer sends one command, `{"cmd":"file_as","strip":"{strip}","as":"{like}"}`: the engine moves the values onto {like}, patch for patch in the order and direction the reading was taken (spectral values too), leaves {strip} unread (since 4.3.8 beta 4: gives {strip} back the valid reading it had before the swipe, when it had one, §11b-2), writes the measurement file at once and puts the reader on {strip}. Its `strip_filed_as` event carries the reading under {like}'s locations and {like}'s expected colours, and the Measure tab judges it exactly as a reading of {like} taken with the reader on {like}: a second reading of {like}, so the re-read rules of 10.10a apply to it (the same colour as a red earlier reading is yellow). The engine says it understands the command in its `session_start` (`"file_as": true`) and in `--caps`.
* **Only at the engine's strip menu** (review of fd8415715). An instrument reads while the window is open, so the answer can come while the engine is mid-swipe or at a question (a misread's retry, an unexpected response, "Done?"), where it would swallow the command: measured on the replay instrument, the reading stayed under {strip} and {like} kept its old one. The answer is then held and sent at the next strip menu that takes no other key; a measurement that ends before that leaves the reading set aside (ChromIQ's log says so).
* **An engine that does not understand it** (one built before 4.3.5) is never sent it: the answer then does what 4.3.4 did (the reading is set aside and the reader goes to {like}). If the engine refuses the move (`file_as_refused`), the reading stays set aside, as after Re-read, and the reader goes back to {strip} (`MeasureManager._handle_engine_line`, k85 leftover fixed in the regression review of 4.3.5 beta 9: the engine refuses at the menu of the strip after the read, so the reader used to carry on there with {strip} unread; `tests/test_435_i_read_strip_b_counts_as_b.py::test_a_refused_file_as_sends_the_reader_back_as_after_reread`).
* **Re-read strip {strip}:** as in 4.3.4: the reading is set aside unjudged, {strip} counts as unread, and the reader goes back to {strip}, whose next reading replaces it.
* **The closing window's line** for this answer reads "{strip} (like {like}, counted as {like})" (M-MEASURED-SUSPECTS line 12; it said "set aside").
* **…only when the engine really moved the reading** (k85, 4.3.5 beta 9). The line used to say "counted as {like}" for every "I read strip {like}" answer, also when the reading was never moved: an engine built before 4.3.5, a move the engine refused, or one still waiting for the engine's strip menu. Each of those leaves the reading set aside (the rules above), so the line now reads "{strip} (like {like}, not moved to {like}, so not used)" for them (M-MEASURED-SUSPECTS, new last line, proposed). Proved by `tests/test_435_i_read_strip_b_counts_as_b.py` and on screen with the real engine on its replay instrument.
* **The move decides the swipe's direction again, against {like}** (k85, 4.3.5 beta 9). The engine decides a swipe's direction while the reader is on {strip}; on a fixed-order chart it looks for a backward swipe only when {strip} reads differently both ways, so with the reader on a strip that reads alike both ways, {like} swiped backwards was moved onto {like} backwards (replay instrument: ΔE 85 from {like}'s colours). The move now mirrors the row when {like}'s colours fit the mirrored order better, under the rule a reading taken on {like} would get. Every other case measured was already right (40 of 40).
* **Proved** by `tests/test_435_i_read_strip_b_counts_as_b.py`: the four endings on the four chart types, with the patch error limit and with the neighbour check doing the flagging, on a fresh measurement and over an earlier reading of {strip}, against the same reading of {like} taken with the reader on {like}; and the real engine on its replay instrument (the reader on {strip}, the saved `.ti3` holding the reading under {like} and nothing under {strip}).

### 11b-2. Confirmed behaviour — the strip a moved reading came off keeps its earlier reading (4.3.8 beta 4)

**Confirmed by:** Basti, 2026-10-21 (approving while Knut is away), on agent 7's side finding in Knut's run 1 of 2026-10-20: strip V read at 16:01; at 16:06 and 16:07 a swipe made with the reader on V was strip U, Knut answered "I read strip U" both times, and V was left with no reading at all. He ended with Save partial, and the profile was built from 1917 of the chart's 1944 patches without any warning (§3c).

* **When "I read strip {like}" moves a swipe away from strip {strip}, and {strip} had an earlier VALID reading, {strip} keeps that earlier reading** (it gets it back): it counts as read, it is shown and judged as it was before the swipe, and the saved measurement holds it.
* **Only a strip that had no valid reading stays unread**, as in 11b-1.
* This amends 11b-1's "which is unread and still has to be measured" for that case; everything else of 11b-1 stands. The window's line for the button says which of the two it will be (M-STRIP-READ-TWICE-EARLIER, proposed).

### ⏳ Awaiting confirmation — how 4.3.8 beta 4 gives the earlier reading back

**Confirmed by:** *nobody yet.*

* **The engine keeps a copy of what a swipe replaces.** chromiq-chartread files every reading under the strip it is positioned on, so the swipe overwrites {strip}'s reading before anyone is asked. Before every transfer the strip loop now copies the row it is about to overwrite, XYZ and spectral values both, when that row has a reading (`cq_remember_row`). One level: the reading just before the latest swipe of that strip; a move off the strip or onto it forgets the copy.
* **The answer asks for it.** "I read strip {like}" sends `{"cmd":"file_as","strip":"{strip}","as":"{like}","earlier":"keep"}` when {strip} had a valid reading before this swipe: every patch of it read (in this session, or in the file being resumed) and none of it set aside by an earlier "Was a strip read twice?" answer (`MeasureManager._strip_has_valid_reading`, learnt at each `strip_read` before the read map changes). Without `"earlier"` the command does what 4.3.5 did. A reading that was itself set aside (Re-read, or I read strip B, that never came back) is never given back: what the engine holds as the earlier reading is then that set-aside one.
* **The engine moves the swipe onto {like}, puts the copy back on {strip}** (`cq_restore_row`), writes the measurement file at once and stays on {strip}, which is now read. Its `strip_filed_as` event says `"restored":true` and carries {strip}'s reading as `from_patches`; the manager counts {strip} as read and trusted again and compares with it as {strip}'s.
* **The Measure tab never takes it off the screen.** The swipe was held unjudged behind the window (4.3.4 beta 1), so what the preview shows of {strip} is still its earlier reading, judged as it was: outlines, cards, the neighbour check's readings and the yellow memory stay exactly as before the swipe (it is not judged a second time, which would count it as its own re-read), and only the counts and the read map change back when the engine confirms.
* **When it does not come back** (the engine refuses the move, says `"restored":false`, or the measurement ends while the answer waits for the strip menu), {strip} is unread after all and is cleared as after Re-read (`earlier_reading_lost`).
* **The engine says it can** (`"file_as_keeps_earlier": true` in `session_start`, and in `--caps`); an older engine is never asked, and the window then keeps M-STRIP-READ-TWICE's line.
* **Where it applies:** only where the question is asked, ChromIQ's engine in strip mode (§11b, "When it does not run"): fresh or resumed, every chart type, bidirectional (the copy is the row as it was stored, direction already applied), multi-page (rows are counted across sheets). Stock chartread, patch by patch, the whole-sheet modes and guided refinement never ask. The `.confirmed.json` is not touched: {strip}'s patches keep the state they had.
* **Proved** by `tests/test_438_i_read_strip_b_keeps_the_earlier_reading.py` (the real engine on its replay instrument: Knut's sequence twice, a strip with no earlier reading, the old command, a resume; the manager's every way it can end; the Measure tab's state before and after) and on screen.

### ⏳ Awaiting confirmation — how the read-twice check decides

**Confirmed by:** *nobody yet.*

Built in `workflow/strip_read_twice.py` and `MeasureManager._check_read_twice`;
proved by `tests/test_182_strip_read_twice.py` (including the real engine on its
replay instrument) and on screen.

* **The figure**: the median ΔE76 between the new strip and an already
  measured one, trying the strip one patch out either way and in either
  direction, over at least 4 patch pairs, is below **1**, and below **a tenth
  of the new strip's own patch-to-patch variation** (the median ΔE76 between
  neighbouring patches of the strip as read). Measured: different strips at
  least 26 apart on Knut's run2 and run3 (median, with the shift) and the same
  strip read twice under 0.5 (Knut's re-reads); Basti's real misread of
  2026-08-08 (`~/ChromIQ/printer-test`, strip D holding strip C's readings) at
  0.08 to 0.18 in all eight archived copies, which is 0.002 to 0.004 of that
  strip's variation.
* **Comparing with what was measured does not make it immune to the paper.**
  Beta 7's first build used a bar of 3 and no variation test. Simulated on the
  bundled charts (printtarg, ArgyllCMS fakeread through a real profile, a gloss
  and a very-low-chroma matte response, instrument noise): randomised charts
  never asked (0 of 70), but FIXED-ORDER charts (`printtarg -r`, "Preserve
  Patch Order") asked about correctly read strips in 27 of 70 cases, 4 of them
  on gloss, because neighbouring strips of an ordered chart can measure 0.7 to
  3 apart. A bar of 1 alone left 2; with the variation test 0 of 140, while all
  eight real misreads are still caught (review of 6de015eb, 2026-10-03). The
  price: on a smooth fixed-order strip (neighbours about 3.5 apart) a real
  misread is asked about only below 0.35.
* **Never compared with itself.** A strip read again where the reader is (C
  read again with the reader on C) is a legitimate re-read and never asks; only
  a reading the engine filed as D that matches C does.
* **Strips the chart designed alike are never compared** (their device values
  differ by less than 2 on the 0 to 100 scale, with the same shift).
* **What counts as already measured**: the strips the file being resumed holds
  and every strip read in this session, each as last read.
* **When it does not run**: stock ArgyllCMS chartread, patch by patch, and the
  whole-sheet modes (no strip is read); guided refinement (its own navigation
  decides what is read next); and a read chartread's own wrong-strip window
  already asked about (only when `-S` is off).
* **The order of the windows**: the question opens after any measurement window
  already open (for example Strip Read Quickly) has closed, and before
  "Continue to next / Jump to unread"; the move after the read waits for its
  answer. **Re-read strip D** is the default and sends the reader back to D,
  whose new reading replaces this one; **Keep** (or closing the window) keeps
  the reading and lets the move go on. A measurement that ends first takes the
  question with it.
* **One question at a time, about the pair it shows.** A strip read while the
  window is open (the instrument does not wait for it) never changes that
  window's question: a second alarm waits and is asked when the first is
  answered, and a waiting one is replaced only by a newer alarm about the same
  strip.

### ⏳ Awaiting confirmation — a reading asked about is judged only after the answer (4.3.4 beta 1)

**Confirmed by:** *nobody yet.*

**The ruling it is built from:** Knut, 2026-10-10, #182 [6094941512](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6094941512), on beta 17: strips A and B read, the reader on C, strip B read again without clicking B; behind "Was a strip read twice?" all of strip C turned red (a second try: yellow), and after "I read strip B" C stayed red. *"the neighbour check did not take consideration of the warning message "Was a strip read twice?", and should have judged the patches AFTER I answered that window, not before, so that the neighbour check would judge the right strip depending on my answer (the message window gives four button options, where the outcome should be correctly done depending on what is chosen). The test of the neighbour check must be constructed to verify all these choices every time this function is verified."*

**The fault:** the engine files a reading under the strip it is positioned on, and the Measure tab judged it (patch error limit, strip test, neighbour check, the yellow memory, the cards, the progress count) as that strip the moment it arrived, before the question was asked; the answer only moved the reader and told the neighbour check to forget.

How 4.3.4 beta 1 builds it (`TabMeasure._hold_for_read_twice`, `_release_read_twice_hold`, `MeasureManager.read_twice_waiting_strips`):

* **Held until the answer.** A strip reading the question is about (on screen or waiting behind another window) is not judged, drawn or counted while it waits: the preview, the cards, the neighbour check, the yellow and green memory and the progress figure stay exactly as they were before the swipe, so no outline appears behind the window. A newer reading of the same strip, read while it waits, replaces the held one; the answer is about the strip's latest reading, as before.
* **The four ways the window ends.**
  * **Keep, it is strip {strip}**: the reading is judged as strip {strip}, exactly as the same reading with no question would be.
  * **Closing the window** (the X, Escape): the same as Keep, as before.
  * **Re-read strip {strip}**: the reading is never judged. Strip {strip} counts as unread (as before), so its patches show no reading and no outline until it is read again; the engine's reading of {strip} is now the set-aside one, which never reaches the saved file, so an earlier reading of {strip} shown before the swipe is not shown either.
  * **I read strip {like}**: the same as Re-read for the reading: never judged, neither as {strip} nor as {like}. The reader goes to {like}, whose next reading is judged as {like}; the set-aside reading is not given to {like}, because the engine cannot move a reading to another strip and it would not be the one saved. **Superseded in 4.3.5** by Knut's ruling (11b-1): the reading is counted and judged as {like}, the engine moves it there, and the reader stays on {strip}. This is still what an engine built before 4.3.5 does.
* **A measurement that ends with the question open** takes the held reading with it: nothing is drawn, and the overlay is painted from the saved file.
* **The window on the last strip** (review R1 of 4.3.4 beta 1). When the engine says every strip is read while the last strip's reading is still held, whether the chart is finished is decided after the answer: Keep (or closing the window) counts the strip and the "all strips read" window follows; Re-read and I read strip {like} leave the strip unread, and the engine's next "all done" brings it. Before this review the held strip was counted as missing: "Every strip has been read, but 8 patches still have no reading" was written to the log and, after Keep, the finished window never came.
* **A newer reading while the window is open** (review R1). If the strip is read again before the answer and the check finds nothing wrong with the new reading, that reading is the engine's and the one the file keeps, so it is judged at once and is not held; the answer about the older reading then never takes it off the screen. Before this review it was held too, and Re-read or I read strip {like} cleared a strip the saved file still held.
* **The next reading of the strip** after Re-read or I read strip {like} is judged on its own: the set-aside reading was never one of its earlier readings, so it can neither confirm it (yellow) nor be corrected by it (green).
* **Where the window can appear:** only ChromIQ's engine reading strips (§11b, "When it does not run"), fresh or resumed. Proved for every button, with the patch error limit and with the neighbour check doing the flagging, on each of the four chart types (each with its own column of Preferences ▸ Measurement), on a fresh measurement and on one whose strip already had a reading, with the window on the last strip and with a newer reading arriving while it is open: `tests/test_434b1_read_twice_is_judged_after_the_answer.py`.

## 12. The computer stays awake while a measurement runs (Basti, #182 6015495063, beta 12)

#### ⏳ Awaiting confirmation

**Confirmed by:** *nobody yet.*

* **When.** From the moment a measurement session starts (Start Measurement, any reading mode, the engine or stock chartread) until it ends, however it ends: all read, failed, stopped, refused before the instrument was asked anything, or the app quitting. Neither the display nor the system goes to sleep in between; the lid closing still sleeps a laptop.
* **How.** macOS: `caffeinate -d -i -w <ChromIQ's pid>`, which ends by itself with ChromIQ, so no assertion is ever left behind (`pmset -g assertions` shows it while it is held). Windows: `SetThreadExecutionState(ES_CONTINUOUS | ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED | ES_DISPLAY_REQUIRED)`, cleared with `ES_CONTINUOUS`. Linux: `systemd-inhibit --what=idle:sleep` where it exists, otherwise nothing. A failure is logged and never stops a measurement. `core/keep_awake.py`, held by `MeasureManager.start`.
* **No window, no setting.** Nothing is shown; it is not optional. Reading a single patch (spotread) does not hold it.

## 13. Installing a profile: a profile of the same name, and a profile renamed after its build (#182, 4.3.5)

### Confirmed behaviour

**Confirmed by:** Knut, 2026-10-10, #182 [6102031563](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6102031563) (answer 3, to question 3 of [6099862394](https://github.com/itsab1989/ChromIQ/issues/182#issuecomment-6099862394), "Installing replaces an installed profile of the same name without asking. Should ChromIQ ask first?": *"Yes. Ask if user wants to replace existing or cancel to rename the profile before trying to install it again. Giving a new name to the profile, after a profile is built, should still rename that profile file name (and the profile description field inside the ICC profile (if selected the option that the description is same as file name), when clicking the install button."*).

* **Before installing**, when a profile of the same file name is already in the install folder, ChromIQ asks: **Replace** or **Cancel**, so the profile can be renamed and installed again.
* **A profile renamed after it was built** (its description changed) is installed under the new name when Install is clicked, with "Name the installed copy after the description" ticked: the installed file's name and the description inside the installed profile.

### ⏳ Awaiting confirmation — how 4.3.5 builds it

**Confirmed by:** *nobody yet.*

* **Every Install button asks the same question** before writing anything (`ui/install_profile.ask_install_path`, given the file `workflow/profile_builder.install_destination` says the install would write): Build Profile, Apply Calibration, Check & Refine's "Install Profile As Is" and the scanner window.
* **The window is Basti's design (2026-10-11, M-PROFILE-INSTALL-REPLACE approved by him, not asked of Knut) and is shown:** an editable name field, the extension kept; **Replace** while the name is unchanged, **Install** once it is edited (the installed copy only is named so; the project's file keeps its name), Replace again with a line saying so when the new name is installed too; **Cancel** installs nothing. Replace / Install is the default button, Cancel is Escape. With the tick on, a copy renamed there carries the new name in its description too. Names: not empty, none of / \ : * ? " < > |, no control character, no leading dot, at most 100 characters.
* **The renamed profile.** With the tick on, the installed copy is named after the description field as it reads when Install is clicked (as before), and its `desc` tag is now set to the same text (`core/icc_text.set_description`: a v2 profile keeps `textDescriptionType` with the accent in its Unicode field, a v4 one `multiLocalizedUnicodeType`; only that tag, the header's size and the profile ID change). The project's own file keeps its name and its description (Knut's earlier rule for this tick). With the tick off nothing changes: the copy keeps the project's file name and the description the profile was built with.
* **Check & Refine's button** has no description field: it names the copy after the description inside the profile, as before, and asks the same question.
* **The scanner window** installs under the profile's file name, as before, and asks the same question.
* Tests: `tests/test_435_install_asks_before_replacing.py`.

### ⏳ Awaiting confirmation: the tick's default and the installed copy's extension (4.3.8 beta 3, K2)

**Confirmed by:** *nobody yet.*

Knut, 2026-10-20 (mail "Small bug and results from profiling"): run 1 was installed with "Name the installed copy after the description" off, so the copy kept the project's file name, and run 2's Install then found it ("A profile with this name is already installed"). He asked for the tick to be on by default, and for the file name and the description inside to follow the Profile description field for .icc and .icm alike.

* **On by default.** *Approved by Basti, 2026-10-21 (approver while Knut is away): on for everyone who never touched the box.* A new user, or one who never touched it, has the tick on (`core/settings.DEFAULTS["install_named_by_description"]`). A choice made by unticking it is kept.
* **One setting, not per run.** It is an install preference (§1.1 of `per_target_settings.md`, "your setup"): the Guided and Manual boxes and both Install buttons read the same value, it is not written into a run's Build Profile store, and switching runs neither changes nor resets it (measured on screen, run1 → run2 → run1 → run3).
* **The extension is kept.** With the tick on, an `.icm` profile is installed as `<description>.icm` (it became `.icc` before); the plain copy and the install window already kept it.
* A description longer than 100 characters still gives a file name cut to 100 (`MAX_INSTALL_STEM`, the Windows path limit) while the description inside is the whole text.
* Tests: `tests/test_k2_install_named_by_description.py`.

**.icc and .icm with the same name are one name.** *Decided by Basti, 2026-10-21 (approver while Knut is away): "installing X.icm when X.icc is already installed must show the existing window, same as a same-extension clash".* Built in 4.3.8 beta 3, awaiting confirmation like the rest of this block:

* `ui/install_profile.ask_install_path` asks when the file it would write exists OR an installed file has the same stem with the other extension, case not counted (`workflow/profile_builder.installed_twins`). The window is M-PROFILE-INSTALL-REPLACE, unchanged, plus the proposed line naming the installed file.
* **Replace** writes the new file and then removes the other one (`remove_installed_twins`, called by `install_profile_file` and the scanner window), so one profile of that name stays installed. A file that cannot be removed (held open by another program) is left, logged, and never fails the install. **Cancel** changes nothing. A typed name that is installed with the other extension is shown the same way, and Replace treats it the same way.
* The 100-character cut is kept as it is (Basti, 2026-10-21).
* Tests: `tests/test_k2_icc_and_icm_are_one_name.py`.
